title: Understand the workspace
summary: Know the four tabs on a phone and a PC, the operator clock and what a display acknowledgement really means.
text: A Program is a saved plan. A service is one run of that plan. Editing a saved program prepares a future run. Adjusting a running service does not rewrite the saved program or old reports. The app has four main destinations. On a phone they are tabs along the bottom. On a tablet or a PC they sit in a side rail, or across the top of the window, depending on the layout. Tab Use it for Live Start and operate a service or a Quick timer, inspect output, send cues and messages, share to screens or join a service. Programs Create reusable plans, arrange segments, add speakers and private notes, choose what each program shows when it ends, keep a segment library and version history. Reports Review completed services, compare durations, add review notes, export, share and print records. Settings Church profile, appearance, desktop or tablet layout, warnings and alerts, display settings, stage cues, Quick message presets, Screens & devices, LED device management, backups, Settings PIN and About. Example Live screen on a phone: countdown, current segment and operator controls Example app preview · select to enlarge The top of Live Part What it does Logo or mark, top left Your church logo, or the built-in ring-and-cross mark. Select it to open the church profile. App or service name The loaded or running service, or Church Service Timer when none is loaded, with your church's name under it. On Programs, Reports or Settings, select either name to go straight back to Live, whether or not a service is running. Lock controls still stops it. Display chip Where the stage output is going, for example LED simulator , Stage simulator , LED sign or Stage screens . Select it to open Choose display . Choosing and connecting a display are separate from starting a service. Full screen During a service or a Quick timer, shows the stage countdown on this device's own screen. On a phone the button is under the display preview instead. See Second screen and full screen . Mini timer On a PC only, and on every page: shrinks the app to a small window that stays above your slides. See Run the service from a PC . Lock During a service, locks every control and key until you Hold to unlock . ⋮ menu Focused operator view and Ready for service . On a PC it also holds Mini timer , Full screen , Commands and Keyboard shortcuts . Three readings to learn first Reading What it tells you Main progress arc The operator's current segment time, allocation and warning/overtime state. Display preview What the selected output is simulating or last acknowledged. Check its badge and any stale or "Output paused after an interruption" indication. Timing status and Service timing overview Progress against the whole plan ("On time", "45 min behind" and so on); its estimated finish can change with pauses and manual advances. Select the status line for the full overview. A running arc does not prove the sign is receiving updates. Likewise, Controller accepted or Stage screens received means the receiving system acknowledged data; it is not a camera view of what a person can see. Use the labels as well as colour: normal time, warning and overtime have different meanings. In Royal Navy, the normal arc is green while the surrounding theme remains gold; warning is amber and overtime is red. Moving around on a phone or tablet Tap the bar, or swipe left or right anywhere on the page. Each tab keeps its place when you come back to it. While a service is loaded or running, Live stays put: leave it with the bar, and swipe back to it from any other tab. A running-service bar on the other tabs, and Return to Live on Settings pages, take you straight back. Swiping is off while the controls are locked or while programs or reports are being selected; a sideways list or slider still scrolls as before, and a swipe from the very edge of the screen is still Android Back. With reduced motion on, the new tab appears at once. The Back key on Programs, Reports or Settings returns to Live. On Live it asks you to press Back again before leaving the app; during a service it asks for confirmation and explains that the timer keeps running. Moving around on a PC In a window at least 1200 wide and 600 tall, Live fills the window with a desktop layout . A new install starts in Mission control , shown below. Click a tab in the side rail or the header, or click the app or service name at the top left, or your church's name under it, to return to Live. A smaller window uses the phone and tablet layout, and so does the focused operator view. A 10-inch or larger tablet held sideways gets the same layouts; a phone never does. Mission control on a PC: status strip, timer, display preview, seven stage cues and the rundown as a timeline, with the keys listed along the bottom Example app preview · select to enlarge The timer, cues, display preview and rundown are the same ones the phone uses, arranged for a wide screen. The layouts are described in Run the service from a PC , and the keys in Keyboard, clicker and Commands . Three safety rules that hold everywhere Every timer action asks you to confirm before anything changes. That is true of a button, a key, a clicker on a PC and the Commands list. Lock controls blocks all input. Buttons and keys do nothing until you Hold to unlock . Locking never pauses the timer. Blank screen hides the output; it does not pause the service.

title: Get started on Android
summary: Install the app on a phone or tablet, allow what it asks for, keep every device on the same version and choose how it checks for updates.
text: The app runs on phones and tablets with Android 7.0 or later . On the phone, open the download page and download the file ending in .apk . From 0.35.0, the lines under each release's notes say which file is for Android and which is for Windows, and how to install each. Open the downloaded file. Android asks whether to allow installs from your browser or file manager; allow it for this install. Open Church Service Timer . It starts on Live with the LED simulator , so nothing reaches a real stage until you choose a display. Check the version in Settings › About . This guide describes 0.35.0, the next release. Until it is published the download page gives 0.34.0, which does not yet have what the release notes list under 0.35.0. Allow what the app asks for The app asks for each of these only when it is needed. The first three protect warnings during a service. Android asks Why it matters Notifications Shows warnings on the phone, and the lock-screen card with the countdown, Pause and Next. Precise timing Lets a warning arrive at its exact second. Battery optimisation Stops Android pausing warnings while the screen is off. Ready for service shows a Battery row with Allow . Nearby devices or location Lets the app find and rejoin the LED sign's Wi-Fi. Camera Only for Scan QR code instead when joining a service. Settle these before the service, not during it. Live › ⋮ › Ready for service lists anything still outstanding. Keep every device on the same version Update every phone, tablet and PC your team uses together. Program files, backups and sent programs saved by 0.28 or later cannot be opened by 0.27 or earlier. A backup or program file made by 0.34 needs 0.34 or later to open if it holds any of the new cue settings: a screen colour, a banner, Wrap long text , its own screen speed, one of the new effects, long text with Flash or Pulse, or more than six cues. The cues a new install starts with use several of these. A backup or program file in which a program, or the default, is set to end on the Clock needs 0.35 or later to open. Earlier versions need an end screen and refuse the file. Programs and backups you already have are unchanged. A paired phone or tablet still on an earlier version shows every cue in white and full screen, at the LED sign's speed, with the new effects as steady text and the next segment's name without its speaker and length. Check for updates Settings › About › Check for updates asks GitHub whether a newer version has been published. It checks when you tap the row, and sends nothing about you or your church. It never checks by itself unless you switch on Check for updates automatically , described below. The row says What to do You have the latest version Nothing. Version … is available Tap Open the download page , download the .apk and install as above. A phone or tablet never downloads or installs an update by itself. The version you have keeps working, so update when it suits you, not during a service. Could not check. This device may be offline. Try again with an internet connection. The app itself never needs the internet to run a service. Installing a newer version over the old one keeps your programs, reports and settings. Export a backup first all the same; see Protect data and manage the LED device . Check for updates automatically Under Check for updates is a switch, Check for updates automatically . It is off to begin with, so the app contacts GitHub only when you ask. About on a phone: Check for updates, then the Check for updates automatically switch, off, with the line "Once a day, when no service is running. Nothing is downloaded or installed without asking." Example app preview · select to enlarge With the switch on: The app makes the same check by itself, at most once a day : about 30 seconds after it opens, and again when it comes back to standing by. It never checks during a service , a Quick timer, a rehearsal, guided practice or Check this service, while the controls are locked, or on a device that has joined another device's service. When a newer version has been published, Live shows a small notice while standing by, such as "Version 0.35.0 is available". If the check cannot reach GitHub it says nothing and tries again the next day. Tapping Check for updates still says when it could not check. Live on a phone while standing by: an example notice, "Version 0.33.0 is available", with Not now and See update, above the Standing by card Example app preview · select to enlarge On the notice What it does See update Opens Check for updates, after the Settings PIN if one is set. From there you update as described above. Not now Hides the notice for that version. A newer version shows it again. Nothing is downloaded or installed without asking. The notice only tells you; you still choose when to update. It never shows during a service, on a stage screen, on the second screen or in full screen. The switch, and what the last check found, are kept on that phone, tablet or PC, and are not part of backups or program files.

title: Get started on Windows
summary: Install on a Windows 10 or 11 PC, learn what is different from the phone, and update it from inside the app.
text: Church Service Timer also runs on a Windows 10 or 11 PC (64-bit), so a service can be run from the laptop at the media desk. It is the same app as on the phone: the same programs, reports, themes and settings. A backup made on a phone restores on the PC, and the other way round. The Windows app is new. Rehearse on the actual PC, with its projector or screens plugged in, before you rely on it in a service. Install it On the PC, open the download page and download the file ending in windows-setup.exe . From 0.34.0, each release lists the Windows installer and its checksum beside the Android .apk . An earlier release may list only the .apk . From 0.35.0, the lines under each release's notes say which file is for Windows, what to do if Windows shows Windows protected your PC , and that a PC already on 0.34.0 or later can use Download and install instead. Run the installer. Windows may show Windows protected your PC , because the installer is not code-signed. Click More info , then Run anyway . Follow the installer. It installs for your Windows account, so it does not need an administrator password. Tick the desktop icon if you want one. Start Church Service Timer from the Start menu. Some releases also list a file ending in windows-x64.zip . Unzip it anywhere and run church_service_timer.exe ; nothing is installed. The first time it opens The app opens on Live with the LED simulator , so nothing reaches a real stage yet. In a wide window you see the Live home: your programs on the left, the chosen program's order of service in the middle, and the display preview and cues on the right. The Live home on a PC before a service: programs on the left, the order of service with Start service in the middle, the display preview and stage cues on the right Example app preview · select to enlarge The window is yours to arrange. Resize it or move it to another monitor. It reopens where you left it. Only one copy runs. Starting the app again brings the open window to the front. Windows may ask about the network. The first time you share to screens, Windows Defender Firewall asks once whether to allow the app. Allow it on private networks, or phones and browsers cannot reach it. Your data stays when the app is removed. Uninstalling leaves your programs, reports and settings in place for the next install. What is different from the phone On a PC What to know Click, not tap The app's own wording changes to "click", and "press and hold" becomes "click and hold". Keyboard Space, Page Down and other keys run the service. Every timer key asks first. See Keyboard, clicker and Commands . Files Import, export, backups and reports use the usual Windows Open and Save windows. Where the phone says Share, the PC saves the file where you choose. Drag and drop Drag one program file ( .json ) or spreadsheet ( .csv ) from a folder onto the window to import it. It opens in the usual review, and nothing is saved until you confirm. A drop is refused while a service is running or the controls are locked. Open with Right-click a program file, choose Open with , then Church Service Timer. Printing Print opens the Windows print window. It stays awake While a service runs, or screens are shared, the PC does not go to sleep or turn its screen off. If it does sleep, for example when the lid is closed, the timer is still right when it wakes. Closing the window During a service the app asks Close during the service? Closing stops the timer on stage screens and the LED sign, and stops warnings. The service is saved, and opening the app again carries on from the clock. Second screen A projector or monitor plugged into the PC can show the stage full screen, with no network or pairing. See Second screen and full screen . LED sign Wi-Fi Join the sign's Wi-Fi in Windows' own Wi-Fi settings; the app does not switch networks for you. The PC can be on a network cable and the sign's Wi-Fi at the same time. Not on a PC Scanning a QR code with a camera (join with the six-digit code instead; the PC can still show a QR code for phones) and the phone's battery settings. Warnings are silent on a PC At each warning a Windows notification appears and the app's taskbar button flashes. It makes no sound , because a PC is often plugged into the sound system. Warnings & alerts on a PC: automatic warnings, then Alerts on this computer with the notification sound switch off and the countdown in the notification area switched on Example app preview · select to enlarge Under Settings › Warnings & alerts › Alerts on this computer : Row What it does Windows notification at each warning Test shows one now. Windows holds notifications back while Do not disturb is on, and turns that on by itself when the screen is duplicated to a projector. The taskbar button still flashes. Play the Windows notification sound Off to begin with. Turn it on only if you want each warning to play the sound, through whatever the PC's sound goes to. Show the countdown in the notification area On to begin with. See below. These three choices are kept on that computer and are not part of a backup. The countdown beside the Windows clock While a service or Quick timer runs, the app adds its ring-and-cross icon to the notification area, beside the clock. Point at the icon to read the time, for example "Sermon · 12:34 left", "Sermon · 01:10 over" or "Paused · Sermon · 12:34". This works while your lyrics or slides program is in front. Click the icon to bring the app's window forward. The icon only shows the time. It cannot change the service, and it goes when the service ends. Windows 11 puts new icons behind the small arrow beside the clock. Drag the icon out onto the taskbar to keep it in view. If the same PC runs your slides, the Mini timer keeps the countdown and three buttons above them; see Run the service from a PC . Update the PC Settings › About › Check for updates checks when you click it, as on the phone. When a newer version has been published, a PC can fetch and start the installer for you. Check for updates on a PC: a newer version is available, with Download and install beside Open release page Example app preview · select to enlarge Click Download and install . A progress bar shows the download, and Cancel download stops it. The app checks the file against the size and checksum published with the release. A file that does not match is deleted and nothing is installed. The app asks "Install version …?". Click Close and install . Anything you are editing is saved first and offered again when the app reopens. The app closes and the installer opens in its own window. Windows may show Windows protected your PC ; click More info , then Run anyway . Finish the installer and start the app. Your services, programs, reports and settings are kept. What you see What it means Only Open release page That release has no Windows installer. Open the page and download whatever it lists. "Finish or end the service first" An update cannot be installed during a service. End the service, then try again. The download is refused The file did not match what was published. Try again later, or use Open release page . Nothing is downloaded or installed by itself. Update between services, never during one, and update the team's phones and tablets to the same version. Let the PC check by itself, if you like. Under Check for updates, Check for updates automatically is off to begin with. Switched on, the PC checks at most once a day, and never during a service. It works as on a phone; see Get started on Android . About on a PC: Check for updates, then the Check for updates automatically switch, off, with What's new in a pane on the right Example app preview · select to enlarge When the automatic check finds a newer version, the Live home shows a notice while standing by. The Live home on a PC with an example notice above the time of day: "Version 0.33.0 is available", with Not now and See update Example app preview · select to enlarge See update opens Check for updates, after the Settings PIN if one is set. Download and install is there, and still asks before anything is installed. Not now hides the notice for that version. A newer one shows it again. The notice never shows during a service, on the second screen or in full screen.

title: Your first rehearsal
summary: Use guided practice, then rehearse the complete service workflow in the simulator, without touching the stage.
text: Allow about 15 minutes. Use the simulator so no practice cue reaches a real stage. The quickest start is guided practice. On a new install, Live shows a card: "New to this? Practise running a service". Choose Start practice , Not now (hides it until the app is next opened) or Don't show again . You can start it any time from Settings › About › Guided practice . Guided practice: the coach card and a highlighted Start first segment button Example app preview · select to enlarge Practice loads a built-in 17-minute Practice service that runs at 5× speed on the Simulator, so nothing appears on stage. It is never added to Programs, saves no report and leaves your programs, reports and settings alone. If another display is in use, practice asks Practise on the simulator? before switching, and offers to switch back when practice ends. A coach card lists eight steps, ticked off as you do them in any order: start, pause and resume, add and remove 2 min, next and Undo, a cue and the timer, blank and unblank, see overtime, and end. A pulsing ring and a small "Tap" badge show which control the current step needs; it never blocks a tap. Use Skip step or Leave practice at any time. At the end, a summary such as "8 of 8 steps done · about 4 min" offers Practise again , and About shows when this device last practised. Practice cannot start while a service is loaded or running, or on a device that has joined another device's service. Then try the full workflow yourself. A step that says "tap" is a click on a PC. Install the app; see Get started on Android or Get started on Windows . Check Settings › About for its version. This guide describes 0.35.0, the next release. Tap the display chip at the top of Live and choose Simulator . The chip then reads LED simulator , or Stage simulator if you have chosen to simulate a stage screen. On Live choose Start service , then load Quick rehearsal (a Pinned or Recent program card on Live loads straight away). In a wide window on a PC, click the program under Choose a program , then Start service . Loading a program enters Ready ; it does not start the countdown. On a PC, Ready shows your layout's own timer with the first segment's full time, not counting. Review the first and next segment. While Ready, choose Service mode : Live timing · 1× or a Fast rehearsal speed. A program's Service/Rehearsal grouping is not its speed setting. Change swaps in another program without leaving Ready. Select Start first segment . When the display is connected and nothing needs attention, the service starts at once and Undo start is offered for 8 seconds; otherwise a confirmation explains what to check. Tap Pause , confirm, and observe the held timer. Tap Resume , then try Custom to add or remove minutes and seconds. Read the proposed result before confirming. Open Stage & display and tap one prepared Stage cue , such as WRAP UP. It sends immediately. The countdown continues underneath. Choose Show timer to restore the current timer, not the original starting time. Tap Blank screen , then Unblank screen . Blanking hides output; it does not pause the service. Use Next ( Next segment on a tablet or PC) when the current activity is finished. If this was accidental, use Undo while it is available and review the confirmation. Allow a segment to reach zero. Observe the operator's red overtime and the shared At zero display behaviour. Reaching zero does not automatically advance the program. Choose End service and confirm. Live returns to Standing by after the report saves. On the Last service card, tap View last service report . Tap Quick timer on Live, choose 5 min and start it. Notice there is no Ready step. Tap End timer when you have seen it count. See Operate a live service for details. On a PC, run one more rehearsal from the keyboard. Press Space , then Space again, to pause. Press Page Down twice for the next segment. Press ? to see every key. Before a real service, let the app run through it for you. Check this service plays a whole program on the Simulator in about 18 seconds and lists every warning that will fire. See Build a reusable program . You are ready for the next lesson when you can explain: Ready versus running, Pause versus Blank, Show timer versus Next, a Quick timer versus a service, and a display acknowledgement versus a physical check. Fast rehearsal accelerates simulated service time (5×, 10×, 30× or 60×). Reports identify it as rehearsal timing, and duration insights exclude rehearsals. Use normal speed for the supported physical LED countdown.

title: Build a reusable program
summary: Create a reusable plan with segments, speakers, notes and its own end screen; import, share, restore versions and check it before Sunday.
text: Open Programs and tap New program . (With no programs at all, Programs offers Create program and Import .) In Program editor , give the plan a useful Program name ; “Youth sunday” is the example placeholder, not a mandatory name. Choose Service or Rehearsal as its Program group . Use Add segment for each activity, in the order it will happen. Enter a Segment name and set its duration in minutes and seconds, for example 5 min 30 s. Each segment stays within 59 min 59 s. Add a Speaker (optional) and Private operator notes where useful: microphone changes, music cues or an agreed finish instruction. Notes are never shown on the sign. Turn on Protect duration for a segment that time recovery must not shorten. Reorder segments using the drag handles ("Drag the handle to reorder" appears once there are two or more). Review the When the service ends card. Choose End screen or Clock ; see below. The end screen reads "Uses the current default" until you give this program its own. Choose Create program for a new plan, or Save changes after editing. Example practice plan: Segment Duration Speaker / private preparation note Welcome 2 min Host · have microphone 1 ready. Worship 5 min 30 s Worship lead · confirm final song with the team. Message 8 min Speaker · send the agreed wrap-up cue. Closing 2 min Host · confirm announcements before closing. The Program editor for a new program: the name, the Service and Rehearsal group, Add segment, and the When the service ends card set to End screen, showing Hallelujah Example app preview · select to enlarge When the service ends. Each program chooses what every display shows after End service . Choice What the displays show when the service ends End screen The program's end screen text, "Hallelujah" to begin with. Tap the row under the switch to edit its text and style. Clock The time of day, in the 12 or 24-hour format you chose. The card says "No end screen. When you end the service, the sign and stage screens show the clock." The Program editor with When the service ends set to Clock: "No end screen. When you end the service, the sign and stage screens show the clock.", with Use current default beneath Example app preview · select to enlarge Every program keeps its end screen until you choose Clock. Choosing End screen again while the editor is open brings back the text you had. Program details, Programs on a PC and the import review say No end screen and Shows the clock when the service ends for such a program. What Live shows and says when such a service ends is in Finish and hand over cleanly . Open a row in Programs for Program details , with Load into Live and Edit program up front. Its ⋮ menu holds Check this service , Duplicate, Export JSON, Export CSV, Print order of service , Send to paired phone (while one is connected), Version history and Delete program , which asks for confirmation. A duplicate is useful for a special service without overwriting a familiar plan. In the Programs list, the pin icon marks pinned programs, which Live offers first. Press and hold a program (click and hold on a PC) to start selecting; the bar at the bottom then offers Pin , Share , Export and, in red, Delete (with a 10-second Undo). Back or × finishes selecting. Segment library. For segments you use often, such as Offering or Announcements, open the segment in the editor and tap Save to library . It keeps the duration, speaker, notes and protection. From library next to Add segment inserts one into any program, with search. Saving the same name again updates it. Programs › ⋮ › Segment library lists them and removes one, with Undo. Up to 50 are kept. Version history. Each time you save a change, the version before it is kept, up to the last 10. Program details › ⋮ › Version history lists them with what changed (for example “Added “Offering”, +4 min in total”). Tap one to open it as "Earlier version" and choose Restore this version , with Undo. Restoring keeps the current name, and the version it replaces stays in history. Unfinished program edits are saved locally as drafts after a short delay ("Draft saved" appears once you change something). On reopening, choose Restore draft , Discard draft , or Cancel. Restoring is not the same as saving the program. If a save fails, keep the app open and use its retry action. The latest keystrokes can be lost if the app is closed before a pending write completes. Importing. Use Programs › ⋮ › Import programs (JSON or CSV) , or open a program .json or .csv file shared to the app. On a PC you can also drag one file from a folder onto the app's window. Every import goes to a review ("Preview program import") before you choose Import program . File What it carries Program JSON Everything: segments, speakers, notes, protection and end-screen formatting. Simple CSV The header Segment Name,Duration (Minutes) , with an optional Seconds column. Names and durations only. Any other spreadsheet (CSV) Opens Match spreadsheet columns . The app guesses which column is the name, duration, speaker, notes or program, and reads durations written as 5 , 5.5 , 05:30 , 5 min or 90s . A live preview lists every problem by row number. The choice is remembered, so next week's sheet in the same layout needs one tap. Then Continue to review . Current limits are 1 MiB and 200 segments. Export Excel files as CSV first. The LED native countdown has its own limit, explained in Connect the LED sign . Sending a program to another phone. While sharing to screens, Program details › ⋮ › Send to paired phone sends the program to the connected operator and viewer phones you tick (stage screens are left out). Private notes are optional. The other phone shows a "Program received" card with Review . If it already has a program with that name, Update mine replaces it and keeps its current version in Version history; Save as copy adds it with a numbered name. Received programs wait until reviewed, even after leaving the pairing (up to five), and are not included in backups. Programs on a PC In a desktop layout, Programs uses the whole window. Programs on a PC: the program list on the left, Harvest Sunday's segments as a table in the middle, and a summary with Load into Live on the right Example app preview · select to enlarge Column What it holds Left Your programs, with search and the All, Pinned, Recent and Rehearsals filters, and New program under the list. Middle The chosen program as a table: each segment with its time, speaker and private note. Right Load into Live , the shape of the service, its total time, what past services say about the timings, the end screen (or No end screen ) and the warnings. To change a program, click Edit program or double-click a segment. This opens the same Program editor, which shows the running order beside the form: when each segment starts and when the service ends. Changes never touch a service that is already running. The Program editor on a PC: two segments, the When the service ends card set to Clock, and the running order on the right Example app preview · select to enlarge Check this service One button runs a whole program through at high speed on the Simulator, so you can see every automatic warning fire before Sunday. Where When Programs , on a program's ⋮ menu Any time no service is running. Live , beside Start first segment While a service is set up in Ready. Choose Check this service . It starts at once, without the usual question, because it touches nothing real. Watch the Simulator. The check takes about 18 seconds whatever the length of the service, and stops for a moment on each warning so you can read it. Stop check ends it at any time. Read the checklist at the end, then choose Done or Check again . Check complete for Sunday Service: each segment with the warnings that fired, four warnings that could not fire, what happens in overtime and the planned finish Example app preview · select to enlarge The checklist shows, for each segment: every warning that fired, the time left when it did, and where it showed: Operator only or Operator and stage ; any warning that cannot fire , because it is set for the whole of the segment or for longer. A 5:00 warning cannot fire in a 3-minute segment, and does not fire as a 5-minute segment starts; then what the display does if a segment runs over, and the planned finish time. It is a check only. It runs on the LED simulator or the Stage simulator, whichever the Simulator is set to. Nothing is sent to the LED sign, paired or web screens or the second screen, the service set up on Live is left as it was, and no report is saved. It is not available while a service is running, a service started from another device stops it, and locked controls block it. Shared settings travel with the device, not the program Global warnings and At zero settings are shared on the receiving device. Importing a program does not establish an independent set of warning rules for it. Keep exports containing private notes within the operator team.

title: Choose the right display
summary: See every way to show the timer: Simulator, LED sign, phones, tablets, browsers, a second screen or your own screen.
text: There are several ways to put the timer in front of people. This lesson lists them all, so you can pick the right one before the detail in the next three lessons. Every way to show the timer Screen Best use What it needs Lesson Simulator Training, and checking what the stage will show, on your own device. Nothing. It does not send to hardware. This one LED sign A physical red LED countdown and short cues at the front of the church. The supported W2 profile, the sign's Wi-Fi and its connection password. Connect the LED sign Phone or tablet stage screen A large stage countdown, rich Quick messages, screen groups and Seen. The app on that device, pairing, and a network that lets devices reach each other. Pair a phone or tablet Web screen A laptop on a projector, a smart TV or people's own phones following in a browser. Nothing installed; the same Wi-Fi as the host, and a guest or team code. Pair a phone or tablet Second screen (PC only) A projector or monitor plugged into the PC running the service. Windows set to Extend . No network and no pairing. Second screen and full screen Full screen When your own screen is the one people watch: a laptop on a lectern, or a tablet on a stand. A running service or Quick timer. Second screen and full screen Stage screens, web screens, a second screen and full screen all draw the same stage picture: a large countdown on black, with cues, warnings, the clock and a blank screen as you send them. This guide calls them "screens" where the LED sign behaves differently. The time on these screens holds still. Every digit has its own place, as wide as the widest digit, so the time keeps one size and nothing shifts as the seconds change. That is true during the service, in the countdown to a scheduled start, and on the clock shown before it. The time changes size only when it gains or loses a character, such as the + of overtime, or when the screen changes size. On a PC, the Stage simulator, the second screen, full screen and the large time in the mini timer use the app's own font, not Windows' font, so they look the same as on a phone. A web screen uses the browser's own font. Choose display Select the display chip at the top of Live, or Change display , to open Choose display . It asks "Where should your stage output appear?" and offers one destination at a time. Each choice shows what is connected, for example "1 paired · 2 web connected". Choose display with LED sign, Phone, tablet or web screens, and Simulator selected with its Simulate switch Example app preview · select to enlarge Destination The chip then reads LED sign LED sign Phone, tablet or web screens Stage screens, or Waiting for a screen until one joins Simulator LED simulator or Stage simulator LED sign and Phone, tablet or web screens are alternative stage-output destinations . Sharing to viewers, operators and web screens is separate, so sharing does not itself replace the LED sign. A second screen and full screen are separate too: they work whichever destination is chosen. Changing destination keeps the service timer running and stops LED reconnect attempts when another destination is chosen. When leaving a connected LED sign, choose whether to Blank previous sign or Leave output . A sign left displaying a countdown can continue on its own. What the Simulator simulates With no LED sign and no stage screens in use, the Display preview on Live shows a pretend display. You choose which kind: Choice The preview shows The chip reads LED sign The exact 32 × 16 LED layout. A new install starts here. LED simulator Stage screen The large countdown, cues, clock and blank screen as a phone, tablet, web or second screen would show them. Stage simulator Change it in either place: In Choose display , under Simulator: Simulate: LED sign | Stage screen . On Live, select the chip beside Display preview and choose Simulate an LED sign or Simulate a stage screen . Live on a PC with the Stage simulator: the Display preview shows the large stage countdown instead of the LED layout Example app preview · select to enlarge Nothing is asked when you switch. The choice is kept on that device and is not part of backups. Locked controls cannot change it. The Stage simulator can also show what a stage screen set to Timer and segment name or Timer and up next would show. Choose it under Simulate in Choose display. This too is kept on that device. Scrolling cues move smoothly on the Stage simulator. The LED simulator moves a whole column at a time, as the sign does. Check the real screen Always check the badge after changing output. A simulator preview, an authenticated LED connection and an acknowledged stage screen are different states. Use Test screen (or Test 5 s in the Quick message composer) and have someone confirm the intended physical screen before the service. If a phone, tablet, PC or browser joins as a stage screen while your display is set to the Simulator or the LED sign, it has nothing to show. Live then shows a note with a Show on stage screens button, which sends the timer to those screens in one step. The waiting screen itself says what to do on the host.

title: Connect the LED sign
summary: Join the right Wi-Fi, authenticate the supported W2 and understand its limits.
text: The hardware path has been tested with Huidu W2, firmware V6.02.232, 32 × 16 red monochrome . Do not assume every LED sign or every W2 firmware is supported. The app reads and validates the profile before publishing content. Power the sign and choose LED sign in Choose display. The Connect the LED sign page walks through three steps. Join the sign's Wi-Fi : connect the operator phone to the sign's network in Android ( Wi-Fi settings ), then come back. On a PC, join it in Windows' own Wi-Fi settings; the app opens them for you but does not switch networks itself. Choose the sign : tap Scan for displays and select the intended display. Sign in : enter its connection password (the field is labelled "Display device password"; it may differ from the Wi-Fi password). Leave Remember password on this phone ("on this computer" on a PC) checked if this is a trusted operator device. It remembers the connection password, not the Wi-Fi password. Tap Connect selected display and check the successful result and preview status. Start a normal-speed service when ready. If restoring a service already in progress after an interruption, review its timer and use Restore current output when offered. Connecting alone does not overwrite what the sign is currently showing. The stored connection password is encrypted on the device: with Android Keystore on a phone, and with Windows' own protection, tied to your Windows account, on a PC. It is left out of backups unless you choose to include saved passwords, encrypted with a passphrase. Forget this sign (in LED device management) removes the app's remembered information and saved passwords; it does not reset the sign. There are two different passwords: Password Where it is used Wi-Fi password Android or Windows uses it to join the sign's wireless network. Connection password The app uses it to authenticate to the LED controller. Supported native countdowns run up to 59:59 . The sign runs an accepted countdown independently and settles at 00:00. The app handles shared At zero output and future segment changes. A brief blink at pause, resume, cue, warning or program replacement is expected on the tested controller; normal counting between replacements should be smooth. The LED sign keeps a steady colon; the blinking colon is for paired and web screens. On a PC. The PC can stay on a network cable while it joins the sign's Wi-Fi, so web screens and the sign can run together. The Tinos font is drawn slightly differently on Windows, most visibly at Short 7 px; check a Tinos cue on the real sign after moving from a phone to a PC. An uploaded countdown can continue if Wi-Fi is lost. A static pause frame or cue may instead remain visible until it is replaced. Do not infer that the sign is current just because it is still lit. Read connection recovery before using automatic recovery during a service.

title: Pair a phone or tablet
summary: Approve stage screens and operators, show who is up next, open web screens in a browser, and manage saved devices.
text: Use one device as the host . It owns the clock and saved data. The host can be a phone, a tablet or a PC. Other phones, tablets and PCs join as stage displays, viewers or additional operators; browsers can follow as web screens. Network first: put the devices on the same Wi-Fi or on the host device's own hotspot. Internet is not required. Some sign hotspots, guest Wi-Fi and church networks keep devices apart ("client isolation"), so phones on them cannot reach each other; the app's advice is then to use the host device's hotspot. QR codes do not bypass isolation. If the host moves to another network while sharing, for example when you turn its hotspot on, it shares again at the new address by itself; approved devices, the team code and joined browsers carry over. Screens & devices on a phone before sharing: Share to screens and Join a service, then Requests from the stage and Full screen on this phone with its three choices Example app preview · select to enlarge On the host, tap Share to screens on Live (or Settings › Screens & devices ). From Choose display › Phone, tablet or web screens, the button is Share to stage screens , which also turns on stage output. Sharing to screens alone keeps LED output. On the joining device, tap Join a service on Live. Give it a clear Device name and choose Use this device as : Service viewer , Stage display or Additional operator . Select the host under Nearby hosts and enter its six-digit code , including leading zeros, then Join service . Alternatively, use Scan QR code instead with the host's Show QR code . A PC has no camera scanning, so it joins with the code; it can still show a QR code for phones. The host reviews and Approve s the joining device. Knowing the code is not enough by itself. A stage display opens in landscape full screen. Tap to reveal its overview and exit tools ( Back to service overview , Open stage display ). Check the host's Saved devices list and use Test screen before going live. Return to Live leaves Screens & devices without ending sharing. On a PC. Screens & devices has three areas: phones and tablets with the app, this computer (its second screen ), and browsers without the app. Join a service is three numbered steps: choose the host, name this device, enter the code. The first time the PC shares, Windows Defender Firewall asks once; allow the app on private networks or other devices cannot reach it. If a stage screen joins and shows only a waiting message , your display is still set to the Simulator or the LED sign. Live shows a note with Show on stage screens ; select it to send the timer to them. When joining, a phone can offer Rejoin this Wi-Fi automatically : it notes the network it is on (church Wi-Fi, the host's hotspot or the sign's Wi-Fi) and rejoins only that network if the link drops. Codes expire after ten minutes. If a code expires or its attempts are exhausted, use New code on the host. A new code does not remove already approved devices. Never publish a live pairing code or QR image in training materials. Role Capability and privacy Host Owns timing, reports and output; approves devices and can take back control. Keep it powered and connected. Additional operator Initially observes and can Request control ; the host must explicitly Give control . Only one operator controls at a time. Private notes become visible when control is granted. Service viewer Observes service information without control or private operator notes. Stage display Shows large timer/cue/message content; no private notes or prepared-cue library. Handing over control does not move the service to the other phone. If that operator disconnects, control returns to the host. Reconnection does not silently restore its control grant. For each saved screen, use Screen options to set a recognisable name, a Screen group ( General, Preacher, Choir, Media desk ) and a Screen layout ( Timer only , Timer and segment name or Timer and up next ). The host can choose which acknowledged screen to inspect in the preview. In a desktop layout, the screens list under the display preview keeps a paired screen that stops answering as "not answering", shows one you disconnected as "disconnected", and counts people following the order of service on the web on one line. Up next on stage. A screen set to Timer and up next says who is next and for how long, on one line under the countdown, such as "Next: Response · Worship team · 6 min 30 s", so the band or the next speaker can get ready. A stage screen set to Timer and up next: the countdown at 12:34 with "Next: Response · Worship team · 6 min 30 s" beneath it Example app preview · select to enlarge The speaker is left out when a segment has none, and a line too long for the screen ends in "…". The line is not shown on the last segment or during a Quick timer. The same three choices, in the same words, are offered everywhere a stage screen is set up: each paired phone or tablet, web stage displays, the second screen on a PC, full screen on the host, and the Stage simulator. A paired phone or tablet still on an earlier version shows only the next segment's name. Disconnect keeps a device saved but pauses its service access. Reconnect on the host can restore it without another code when the receiver app is available on the same reachable network. Forget device revokes approval and requires pairing again. If the receiver deliberately leaves, it must choose Reconnect saved host to rejoin. Stop sharing is deliberate; host sharing does not automatically restart on app launch. One host with three stage receivers is within the current eight-connection cap for paired devices, which also counts pending connections. That cap is not a guarantee of performance on every router or phone; rehearse the exact setup. Web screens in a browser While sharing, Settings › Screens & devices › Web screens shows three ways for a browser on the same Wi-Fi to open the page: Easy name , made from the church name, for example grace-community.local:8080 . iPhones, iPads, Macs and most laptops open it; some Android phones do not. Change easy name edits it. QR code , which any phone camera reads. Address , the host's own address such as 192.168.1.23:8080 , as a last resort. Browser view Shows Needs Order of service The rundown with the current item marked NOW ; no times. Speakers only if Show speakers in the order of service is on. The guest code (4 digits, the same each week until you tap Change guest code ), or nothing if set to open. Stage display The full-screen countdown, cues and Quick messages. The team code . Service overview Time left, ahead or behind, finish time and the rundown with durations and speakers. The team code . Stage displays show , under Web screen options , sets what every web Stage display shows under the countdown: Timer only , Timer and segment name or Timer and up next . It applies to all of them at once. The 6-digit team code changes each time you share, or with New team code , and unlocks switching between all three views. Order of service access can be Off , Needs the guest code (the default) or Open to anyone on this Wi-Fi . Changing a code signs out the browsers that used the old one. No browser can control the service or see private notes. Export join slide makes an image with the church name, a large QR code, the easy name, the guest code and the address, ready to project. Pick the screen it is for (16:9 HD or 4K, 16:10, 4:3, Portrait 9:16 or Square) and dark or light. If the host's address changes afterwards, the panel says the slide is out of date: export it again. A printed address or QR stops working if the router gives the host a new address, so ask for the address to be reserved on the router, or show the join slide instead. A browser shows a red "Connection to the host device lost · reconnecting…" banner and fades the countdown within about five seconds of the host going quiet, and picks up again by itself when the host returns. On a web Stage display, the Full screen chip becomes Exit full screen . Requests from the stage When Requests from the stage is switched on in Screens & devices (off by default), a presenter can quietly ask the operator for something during a service, from a paired stage screen or a team-code web Stage display. A small Request button offers three fixed choices: Need 2 minutes , Ready to finish and Microphone issue ; there is no free text. How the operator answers is in Operate a live service .

title: Second screen and full screen
summary: Show the stage on a projector or monitor plugged into the PC, or fill your own screen with the countdown and run the service from it.
text: Two ways to show the stage countdown without pairing anything. A second screen is a projector or monitor plugged into the PC. Full screen uses the screen of the device that is running the service. Show the stage on a second screen (PC) Plug the projector or monitor into the PC. Press Windows + P and choose Extend . With Duplicate, Windows sees only one screen, so there is nothing to show the stage on. On Live, look under the Display preview. A line says what the second screen is doing: "Second screen: not showing". Click Show on second screen . The stage fills that screen, with no title bar or taskbar. With more than one extra screen, choose which from the list beside the button. The line now reads, for example, "Showing on Screen 2 · 3840 × 2160", and the button becomes Stop . Live on a PC while the stage shows on a second screen: the Display preview holds a live copy, with "Showing on Screen 2" and a Stop button beneath it Example app preview · select to enlarge The second screen shows what a paired stage screen shows: the countdown, prepared cues, automatic warnings, messages from Send message , the clock and a blank screen. It needs no network or pairing, and it works whichever display you have chosen, the LED sign included. To stop , click Stop , press Esc on that screen, or unplug it. Closing the app closes it too. With no extra screen connected, the line reads "No second screen connected" and there is no button. Lock controls disables the button like every other control. Show on second screen is also in Commands ( Ctrl+K ). See the second screen on Live While the second screen is showing, the Display preview on Live holds a small live copy of it, in that screen's shape and layout. Your display Where the copy appears Simulator It takes the Simulator's place, and the chip beside Display preview reads Second screen . LED sign, or phone, tablet or web screens Their preview stays. The copy sits under it with its own Second screen heading. When the second screen stops, the preview goes back to how it was. Second screen settings Settings › Screens & devices › Second screen has the same Show and Stop for each screen, and two more choices. Screens & devices on a PC: phones and tablets with the app on the left, this computer's Second screen card in the middle, and web screens on the right Example app preview · select to enlarge Setting What it does Open the second screen when a service starts Off to begin with. When on, starting a service or a Quick timer shows the stage on the screen you last used. If that screen is not connected, nothing opens and Live says so. It never opens on your own screen by itself, and guided practice does not open it. What the second screen shows Timer only , Timer and segment name , or Timer and up next . This is the second screen's own choice; paired stage screens keep theirs. The app remembers the screen you last showed the stage on and offers it first next time. After changing the resolution or the arrangement of screens in Windows, click Show once to choose it again. These choices are kept on that computer and are not part of a backup. Ending the service leaves the second screen open, showing the program's end screen, or the clock if the program has no end screen. Close it with Stop when the room no longer needs it. Full screen on the device running the service Use this when your own screen is the one people watch. During a service or a Quick timer, Live can replace itself with the stage picture: the big countdown on black, with warnings and cues as they appear on stage. To open it Where The Full screen button At the top right of Live on a tablet or PC; under the display preview on a phone. ⋮ › Full screen The Live menu. F11 On a PC. Full screen in Commands On a PC, with Ctrl+K . To leave , press Esc or F11 , or tap or click once and choose Exit in the tray that comes up. A small Exit full screen control also shows at the top right for the first few seconds. On Android, Back leaves it too. While the tray is showing, Esc or Back puts the tray away first; press it again to leave. Full screen does not leave by itself when the service ends. It stays on the end screen, or the clock; see When the service ends below. A phone or tablet turns sideways. On Android, full screen turns the stage picture to landscape, either way round, so the countdown is as large as it can be. When you leave full screen, the phone or tablet goes back to turning as it did before. A PC is unchanged. Nothing changes in what the LED sign, a second screen or paired screens receive. Running the service from full screen You can run the whole service without leaving full screen: with gestures, with a small tray of controls, or with the keys on a PC. The same safety rules hold as on Live. Gestures. Double tap, or double-click, one third of the screen. Where It asks to Left third Undo the last segment change. With nothing to undo, a short "Nothing to undo" shows and fades. Middle Pause , or Resume when paused. Right third Go to the Next segment . On the last segment, a short "This is the last segment" shows and fades. Each gesture asks first , in the same small card the keys and buttons use. Nothing changes until you confirm, so a stray double tap can be cancelled. Full screen on the device running the service: the countdown and the up next line dim behind a small card asking "Pause Sermon?" with Cancel and Confirm pause Example app preview · select to enlarge The control tray. A small tray along the bottom holds the controls. To bring it up: tap or click once anywhere. It waits a moment, so a double tap is not taken for it; swipe up from the bottom edge of the screen; on a PC, move the mouse to the bottom of the screen. Full screen on a PC with the control tray along the bottom: Pause, Next, −2 min, +2 min, Undo, Cues, Clock, Blank, End service in red, and Exit Example app preview · select to enlarge In the tray What it does Pause or Resume , Next , −2 min , +2 min , Undo The timer actions. Each asks first, as on Live. Cues Lists your prepared cues. Choose one to show it. Choose the one that is showing to go back to the timer. Clock Shows the time of day. The button then reads Timer , which goes back. Blank Blanks the screen. The button then reads Unblank . End service Asks just as it does on Live. For a Quick timer it reads End timer . Exit Leaves full screen. Cues, Clock and Blank do what they do on Live: they change what every display shows, not only this screen. The tray hides after 6 seconds untouched. It stays while the mouse is on it, or while a question from it is open. Esc , Back on Android, or a swipe down puts it away at once. With Reduced motion on, the tray appears without sliding. The tray, the cards and the short messages show on this screen only. Nothing of them is sent to the LED sign, a second screen or paired screens. People watching this screen will see them for a moment. Full screen on a phone held sideways: the countdown with the same control tray along the bottom Example app preview · select to enlarge Keys. On a PC the keys work as they do on Live. Every timer action still asks first , in a small card over the stage. Next segment still needs its second press. With Lock controls on, none of this works. The gestures and the tray do nothing, and every key is blocked, Esc and F11 included. A tap, a click or Esc shows Controls locked and Hold to unlock in place of Exit. When the service ends Full screen stays open, however the service ends. The people watching see the program's end screen, or the clock if the program is set to end on the Clock , not your Live page. The timer buttons in the tray grey out. Cues , Clock , Blank and Exit keep working. With a program set to end on the Clock, Clock in the tray is greyed out, as the clock is already showing. Blank, cues and messages go back to the clock when they are cleared. Leave when the room no longer needs it: Exit in the tray, Esc or F11 . Full screen closes by itself when the next service is set up. Full screen cannot be opened after the service has ended. It needs a running service or Quick timer. What full screen shows The same three choices: Timer only , Timer and segment name , or Timer and up next . Device Where to choose PC It uses the choice made for the second screen, in Settings › Screens & devices › Second screen . Phone or tablet Settings › Screens & devices › Full screen on this phone . It is kept on that device and is not part of a backup. A device that has joined another device's service as a stage screen already has its own full-screen stage display, so it is not offered this one. Full screen cannot be opened from the mini timer.

title: Operate a live service
summary: Start, pause, adjust, advance and blank with clear control, or run a Quick timer.
text: Load the correct program, check its first segment and destination, then Start first segment . Program transitions remain manual: the app does not decide when worship, a message or an announcement is finished. Before you start. In Ready you can: Use Change to swap in another program (pinned first, with search); an 8-second Undo switches back. Set a Pre-service countdown ( Set time ). The time is chosen on a 24-hour clock; on a PC you can type the hours and minutes. The display shows the clock until the last hour, counts down to the start, then holds "STARTING SOON" at 00:00. On screens, that clock and countdown hold still: they do not shift or change size each second. It never starts the service by itself. Tapping Start first segment early asks "Start now?" first. Read the "Last time" review note if the same program has one. Run Check this service , beside Start first segment , to see every warning fire on the Simulator first. See Build a reusable program . Control or reading What to do and expect Pause / Resume Confirm the action. Pause holds the service clock; Resume continues it. LED replacement can blink briefly. −2 min / +2 min Review the confirmation before changing the current segment's time. Custom Choose add or remove and set minutes and seconds. Review the resulting timer; time can continue while the dialog is open. Next (Next segment on a tablet or PC) Confirm when the next real activity begins. It starts that segment's allocation and replaces the previous output. Segment title Tap the current segment's name to Jump to segment further ahead, with a confirmation. Full screen Shows the stage countdown on this device's own screen, where gestures and a control tray run the service. See Second screen and full screen . Undo Reverses the supported last segment change when available; it is not a universal undo of every action. Review the confirmation. "of 10:00 allocated" The current segment's allotted time, not the entire service length. View / Hide operator notes Opens the current segment's private notes; it does not publish them to stage displays. Focused operator view In the ⋮ menu. Keeps essential controls, timer, cues and display preview prominent. Lock controls The lock icon blocks every button and every key. Use Hold to unlock to regain local controls. It does not pause time. Tap a row in Service rundown to inspect its timing, speaker and private note. Opening that information does not advance to the row. The rundown header also holds Edit upcoming , Recover time and a print icon for Print order of service . At zero, the operator view enters Overtime and shows red text while the display stays at 00:00 or the configured At zero text. This is intentional. Start the next segment when appropriate; do not add time merely to hide an overrun from the report. The Stage & display panel holds Stage cues (three across where there is room), Show clock , Send message , Blank screen and Quick timer , plus the display preview. Show clock puts the time of day on the display (12 or 24 hour, set in Display settings › Clock format); Back to clock or Show timer returns. Blank screen is a toggle: tap again as Unblank screen to restore current output. It also works after End service. Timing and phone alerts continue while blanked, but automatic stage warnings are suppressed. The preview should remain present and identify intentional blanking. Lock-screen controls. On a phone or tablet, during a service, a notification shows the current segment with a live countdown (counting up in overtime), with Pause/Resume and Next; Next needs a second tap. It is on by default in Settings › Warnings & alerts › During a service , and it obeys Lock controls. Keyboard, clicker and foot pedal. On a PC, Space, Page Down and other keys run the service, and each timer key asks first. A clicker or foot pedal can drive Live on a phone, tablet or PC. Both are in Keyboard, clicker and Commands . On a PC. While another program is in front, the countdown is beside the Windows clock, and the mini timer keeps it above your slides. Under the display preview, one line and one button show the stage on a projector or second monitor. See Get started on Windows , Run the service from a PC and Second screen and full screen . Requests from the stage. If a presenter sends a request, the phone vibrates briefly and a card on Live shows it with Acknowledge and Dismiss . "Need 2 minutes" also offers Add 2 min , the normal adjustment with Undo; nothing changes the timing by itself. The presenter's screen shows "Sent", then "Seen by operator" or "2 minutes added". One request per screen at a time, at most one every 5 seconds, and requests expire after 2 minutes. The service report lists each request and what you did. Quick timer For a prayer meeting, a break or a talk that isn't a whole service, use Quick timer instead of a program. It is available when no service is loaded or running: on the Standing by card next to Start service , or as the tile beside Show clock, Send message and Blank screen. Choose 5 min , 10 min , 15 min , 30 min or 45 min , or Custom… for any length up to 59 min 59 s. Your last three timers appear under Recent as one-tap choices. Optionally give it a Name (optional) , such as "Prayer meeting". Leave Save as a report off unless you want a record. Off, nothing is saved when it ends; on, it is saved in Reports, marked Quick timer. Tap Start 5 min timer (the button names the length). It starts straight away, with no Ready step. It counts down on the LED sign, stage screens, web screens and a second screen together, with Pause, ±2 min, overtime, warnings, full screen and the lock-screen controls as usual. End timer stops it and shows the default end screen, or the clock if the default is set to Clock. Saved Quick timers are left out of service averages and length suggestions.

title: Run the service from a PC
summary: Choose a desktop or tablet layout, read the Live home and Ready before a service, and keep a mini timer above your slides.
text: In a wide window, on a PC or a 10-inch or larger tablet held sideways, Live fills the screen instead of scrolling one column of cards. Everything works as in Operate a live service : every timer action still asks first, and Lock controls still blocks them all. This lesson covers what the wide screen adds. The Live home, before a service With no service loaded, a wide window shows three areas. Area What it holds Left: Choose a program Your programs. Click one to see it in the middle. Edit programs opens Programs. Middle The time of day, then the chosen program's order of service with each segment, speaker and length, a small Print button beside the summary, and one Start service button. Under it: Quick timer , Share to screens and Join a service . The Last service card follows. Right The display preview and stage cues, already open. Start service opens Ready, where you check the display and start the first segment. Nothing counts until then; see Ready in each layout . The picture of this page is in Get started on Windows . Choose a desktop layout Settings › Desktop layout lists five layouts. (On a tablet the row is Tablet layout ; see below.) Each arranges the same timer, cues, display preview and rundown. Choosing a layout also sets the theme it comes with; you can pick any theme afterwards. Settings › Desktop layout: layout cards for Mission control and Three panes, with a preview beside them and Save appearance at the bottom Example app preview · select to enlarge Layout What it is like Comes with Mission control Everything on one screen, with the rundown as a timeline. A new install starts here. Midnight Lime Three panes Rundown on the left, timer in the middle, stage and cues on the right. Midnight Lime The dial The whole service as a ring, with the countdown inside. Royal Navy Keys Dense and keyboard-first: the timer in a strip, the rundown as a table. Graphite Classic One column of cards, as on a tablet. Your current theme Click a layout, then Save appearance . If you already used the app before Mission control became the starting layout, your layout stays as it is. A window narrower than 1200 or shorter than 600 uses Classic, the phone and tablet layout, whatever layout is chosen. So does the focused operator view. Windows display scaling makes the window smaller than the screen. A 1920 × 1200 screen at 150% gives the app about 1270 × 790, which is wide enough for every layout. A 1366 × 768 screen at 125% gives about 1093 × 614, which is under 1200 wide, so the app uses Classic. On a tablet The same setting is called Tablet layout on an Android tablet, with the line "Used when the tablet is in landscape". Appearance on a tablet: the Layout & accessibility tab with Tablet layout, and Mission control and Three panes to choose from Example app preview · select to enlarge Device What Settings shows PC Desktop layout . Tablet of 10 inches or more Tablet layout . It is used with the tablet in landscape and the app filling the screen. In portrait or split screen, Live keeps the phone layout. 7 or 8-inch tablet, or a phone Nothing. The screen is never wide enough, so Settings, Settings search and Appearance do not offer a layout. Saved looks and keyboard keys on buttons are still there. The layout you had already chosen is kept. Mission control For seeing the whole service at a glance. Mission control on a 2560 × 1440 monitor: a larger ring, and a taller timeline whose blocks add the speaker, the planned time and how long each segment took Example app preview · select to enlarge The strip across the top says how far ahead or behind the service is, the time now, the time elapsed, the planned finish and when it is now set to end, with End service beside it. The timer, the display preview and the cues sit side by side. The rundown is a timeline along the bottom. Each segment is as wide as the time it takes. Finished segments show how long they really took, with the part that ran over marked. A line shows where the service is now. Click a segment for its details. The keys that work on Live are listed along the bottom edge, J Jump to segment among them. In a tall window it also lists the screens that have joined, under the display preview, and the service's latest activity, under the cues. Three panes The whole rundown is on the left, with how long each finished segment really took and how far ahead or behind the service is running. The timer and its controls are in the middle, with the private note in view. The display preview, cues and messages are on the right. Live, Programs, Reports and Settings become tabs in the header. The keys are listed along the bottom of the middle pane, as they are in The dial, wherever there is room: on every common screen from 1280 × 720 up. Three panes in the Paper & Ink theme: rundown on the left, a large countdown ring in the middle with the keys listed beneath it, display preview and stage cues on the right Example app preview · select to enlarge The dial Built around the app's own mark. The whole service is a ring, with a piece for each segment, running round to end at the cross. Finished segments fill in, with any overrun marked. Inside it, a second ring shows the time left in the running segment, with the countdown in the middle and the time the service is now set to end beside the cross.
