title: Keyboard, clicker and Commands
summary: Every key that works on Live, the Commands list, and how to test a clicker or foot pedal.
text: On a PC the whole service can be run from the keyboard. Two rules hold for every key: Every timer action asks you to confirm before anything changes. Lock controls blocks every key until you hold to unlock. Ctrl L locks; it cannot unlock. Keys on Live Keys What it does How it confirms Space or B Pause or resume Asks first Page Down or → Next segment Press twice to confirm + or − Adjust time You choose, then confirm Ctrl Z Undo the last segment change Asks first J Jump to a later segment You choose, then confirm R Recover time You choose, then confirm E Edit upcoming You edit, then save Ctrl L Lock controls At once; hold to unlock 1 to 9 Show a prepared cue At once; press again to go back to the timer M Send message You type, then send Ctrl K Commands A list of everything you can do now Ctrl M Mini timer A small window on top; press again to leave it F11 Full screen The stage on this screen; press again, or Esc, to leave it ? or F1 Keyboard shortcuts Opens the list of keys Enter or Space Confirm the question on screen Not End service, which must be clicked Esc Cancel or close Nothing is changed Pausing takes two presses. Space asks, for example, “Pause Sermon?”; a second Space , or Enter , confirms; Esc cancels. End service and the other destructive questions must be clicked, so a stray key can never end a service. When the keys work Timer and stage keys (from Space down to M in the table) work on Live while a service is running, with no question or other page on top. The cue numbers and M also need a display connected. Ctrl Z needs a segment change to undo. J needs a later segment to jump to. Ctrl K and ? work on any tab, but not under a dialog. Ctrl M works on every page, with or without a service. F11 works whenever a service is running. In full screen, the timer and stage keys work as they do on Live, and Esc puts the control tray away first if it is showing. Full screen also has gestures and a tray for a mouse or a touch screen; see Second screen and full screen . Space , B , Page Down and → follow the Clicker and foot pedal switch; see below. No key does anything while you are typing in a field. A question mark typed into a field is still a question mark. The + key works without Shift, and the number pad's keys work too. The shortcuts list Press ? or F1 to see every key and what it does, grouped as During a service , Stage and Moving around . It is also under Keyboard shortcuts in Commands, in the Live ⋮ menu and in Settings search. Esc closes it. It does not open while the controls are locked. The Keyboard shortcuts list on a PC, grouped as During a service, Stage and Moving around, with the two safety rules at the top Example app preview · select to enlarge Commands Press Ctrl K , or choose Commands in the ⋮ menu on Live, to open a list of everything you can do right now. Start typing, for example "pause", "wrap up" or "settings". Use the arrow keys to move, and press Enter to choose. Esc closes the list. What is most likely needed is suggested first, such as Recover time when the service is running behind. Each command shows its key. A command is listed only while its button would work, and anything that changes the timer still asks you to confirm, exactly as its button does. Commands on a PC: a search box, Recover time suggested first because the service is behind, then timer commands with their keys Example app preview · select to enlarge Clicker and foot pedal A clicker or pedal works like a small keyboard: each button sends one key. The clicker sends On a PC On a phone or tablet Page Down or Right arrow Next segment: press twice to confirm Next segment: press twice, within 4 seconds, to confirm B or Space Pause or resume: asks first, and Space or Enter confirms Pause or resume at once, without asking Page Up, Left arrow, F5 and others Nothing Nothing One switch turns these keys on or off on every device: Settings › Warnings & alerts › During a service › Clicker and foot pedal . It is on to begin with. On a phone or tablet a clicker's pause acts at once, because there is no screen in the hand to confirm on. Give the clicker only to someone who understands that. On a PC the switch works too. Turn it off when a stray pedal, or the clicker that drives your slides, would otherwise reach the timer. A PC cannot tell a clicker from its keyboard. With the switch off, Space , B , Page Down and → do nothing from the keyboard either. With the switch off on a PC What happens Space, B, Page Down and → Do nothing on Live, from a clicker or the keyboard. The buttons on screen Still work, and still ask first. +, −, Ctrl Z, M, the number keys and the other shortcuts Still work. The Pause and Next buttons, the line of keys and Commands Stop showing Space and Page Down. The shortcuts list and Test a clicker or pedal Say those keys are switched off. Test a clicker or pedal Before the service, find out what each button really sends. Open Settings › Warnings & alerts › Test a clicker or pedal . Press each button on the clicker or pedal. The page names the key ("Page Down", "Right arrow", "F5") and says what that key does on Live, or that the app does not use it. It keeps the last few presses. Test a clicker or pedal on a PC: the last press was Page Down, which is Next segment, beside a list of what a typical clicker sends Example app preview · select to enlarge Nothing pressed on that page reaches a running service , so it is safe to test mid-service. The page works on phones, tablets and PCs. Many pedals can be set to send a different key with the maker's own program.

title: Prepared cues and automatic warnings
summary: Prepare one-tap instructions, give them an effect and a look for screens and the sign, and set warnings by time remaining.
text: Prepared Stage cues are short reusable instructions such as WRAP UP or SPEAK UP. Configure them before the service in Settings › Stage cues , or use the Manage cues link on Live. Create or edit a cue's text, choose Bold or Italic , and pick an Effect . Then set how it looks on the LED sign and on screens; see below. Save it. The Live cue buttons share this saved set across services. During the service, tap the cue once to send . On a PC, the keys 1 to 9 send the first nine cues, and pressing the number of the cue that is showing goes back to the timer. There is no editing step on Live; choose deliberately. Before a service starts, Stage cues says "Cues work once the service starts". Select Show timer when the instruction has served its purpose. The timer has continued beneath the cue. Changing the saved cue later does not rewrite content already on stage. Deleting an individual cue or warning offers an eight-second Undo , preserving its formatting. This Undo does not apply to deleting reports. Stage cues in Settings on a phone: the seven cues a new install starts with, each with a line saying how it shows on the sign and on screens Example app preview · select to enlarge The cues you start with A new install has seven cues, on keys 1 to 7. They are a starting set: change them, delete them or add your own. Key Cue On screens On the LED sign 1 WRAP UP Amber banner at the bottom, pulsing A word at a time 2 TIME'S UP Red, full screen, flashing Flashes, a word at a time 3 SPEAK UP White banner at the top Scrolls 4 SLOW DOWN White banner at the top Scrolls, a little slower 5 MIC OFF? Amber banner at the top Scrolls 6 FINAL SONG Green banner at the bottom Scrolls 7 SEE ME Your theme's colour, full screen, sliding in Scrolls On the LED sign they use the tall 14-pixel letters, which read best from a distance. On screens each is set to wrap, so it holds still and is as large as fits. If you already use the app , the earlier WRAP UP, TIME'S UP and MIC LOW, where still as they came, are replaced by these seven, followed by any cues you added. Cues and warnings you changed are left alone. Effects The Effect list says what each effect does. The names that end in "(must fit)" need text short enough for the LED sign. The Effect list in the cue editor: Static (must fit), Scroll long text, Flash, Flash then hold (must fit), Pulse, Slide in and Countdown bar, each with a line saying what it does Example app preview · select to enlarge Effect On screens On the LED sign Static (must fit) Holds still. Holds still. The text must fit. Scroll long text Moves across. Moves across. Flash Blinks on and off until cleared. The same. Long text shows a few words at a time. Flash then hold (must fit) Flashes three times, then stays steady. The same, and flashes three times again every 5 minutes while the cue stays up. The text must fit. Pulse Gently brightens and dims, about every two seconds. The sign cannot dim, so it shows the text steady. Long text shows a few words at a time. Slide in Slides in from the bottom edge as it appears, then holds still. A banner slides in from its own edge. Steady, or scrolls if too wide. Countdown bar A thin bar in the cue's colour, just under the words, empties as the cue's time runs out. Steady, or scrolls if too wide. Screen flash Washes the whole screen once with a deep shade of the cue's colour (red for a white cue) as it appears, then settles. In a banner only the band flashes. Steady, or scrolls if too wide. Long text with Flash or Pulse. Text too wide for the sign is split into groups of whole words that fit, shown one after another, over and over. "PLEASE WRAP UP NOW" may show as "PLEASE", then "WRAP", then "UP NOW". Screens step through the same groups at the same time, unless Wrap long text is on, when they show the whole message at once. This works for up to 60 characters; for longer text the editor suggests Scroll long text . A single word too wide for the sign still has to be shortened. Slide in, Countdown bar and Screen flash are for screens. The LED sign cannot draw them, so it shows the cue steady, or scrolls it at Speed on the LED sign when the text is too wide. The countdown bar needs a time to count. That is a warning's time, or the time chosen when a cue is sent for a set time. A cue shown until cleared has no bar. Reduced motion. With it on, a cue that slides in simply appears, and Screen flash gives the screen a coloured edge instead of a flash. The countdown under a banner never moves or changes with any effect. One editor, two displays Over the editor's preview is a small switch, LED sign | Stage screen . It starts on the display you are using. It changes the preview, and it also chooses which settings the editor shows. A line under the switch says which. The cue editor on Stage screen: the LED sign and Stage screen switch over a preview of AMEN, with a line saying the settings shown are for the stage screen Example app preview · select to enlarge The switch is on The editor shows LED sign The group On the LED sign : the display font, Tall · 14 px (switch it off for the shorter 7-pixel letters), the alignment and Speed on the LED sign . Stage screen The group On screens : colour, position, Wrap long text and Speed on screens . Either The text, Bold , Italic and Effect . These change both displays. Nothing is lost by switching: the hidden settings are kept and saved. Editing a warning's text has the same switch, so a warning can have its own effect, colour, banner and screen speed. How a cue looks on screens The LED sign is small, red and one colour. Stage screens, web screens, a second screen and full screen are large and can do more. The On screens group is for them. Nothing in it changes the LED sign. The cue editor's On screens group: Colour set to Amber, Position set to Banner at the bottom, Wrap long text switched off and Speed on screens at 30 Example app preview · select to enlarge Setting Choices Colour White (as before), Amber , Red , Green or Theme colour . Position Full screen : the cue takes the place of the countdown. Banner at the top or Banner at the bottom : the cue shows in a band and the countdown, or the clock, stays in view. Wrap long text Shows the cue on up to 3 lines (2 in a banner), centred and as large as fits, instead of scrolling it or shrinking it onto one line. A scrolling cue then holds still on screens while the LED sign keeps scrolling it. Speed on screens How fast a scrolling cue moves on screens, up to 48, twice the sign's fastest. Until you move it, screens follow the sign. Same as the LED sign puts it back. Keep wrapped text short. Text that would be too small to read on 3 lines scrolls instead, so nothing is cut off. With more than 60 characters the editor warns that long text is hard to read from a distance; you can still save it. A banner keeps the countdown in view. A stage screen showing the countdown at 12:34 with WRAP UP in an amber banner at the bottom Example app preview · select to enlarge A banner needs a running service to sit over. After the service has ended, a banner cue fills the screen. Bold, italic and every effect work in a banner too. A coloured cue that fills the screen sits on a warm charcoal background with a band of its colour along the bottom edge. Red, Green and Theme colour cues have their words in that colour; Amber cues have warm white words. White cues stay white on black. A red TIME'S UP cue filling a stage screen: red words on warm charcoal with a red band along the bottom edge Example app preview · select to enlarge Wrap long text and the countdown bar together: A green cue wrapped onto three lines, PLEASE MAKE YOUR WAY TO THE FRONT FOR PRAYER, with a countdown bar half empty just under the words Example app preview · select to enlarge Scrolling cues move smoothly on paired screens, web screens, a second screen and full screen, and carry on from where they were when the host sends an update. In a wide window, the pane beside Settings › Stage cues and beside Warnings & alerts shows every cue and warning as your display will show it: On the LED sign with an LED sign or the LED simulator, and On the stage screen with stage screens or the Stage simulator. Point at a scrolling cue to play it. Settings › Stage cues on a PC: seven cues listed, with a pane on the right showing each one as the stage screen will, including an amber WRAP UP banner, a red TIME'S UP and SEE ME in the theme's colour Example app preview · select to enlarge Cues, backups and program files you already have look the same as before. A paired phone or tablet still on an earlier version shows every cue in white and full screen, at the sign's speed, with the new effects as steady text. Text for the LED sign Switch the editor to LED sign for these. Choose I-Proton Matrix , I-Proton Sq-Matrix , or bundled Tinos . Matrix countdown digits are unchanged. Tinos has regular, bold, italic and bold-italic faces; no font import is needed. Tall 14 px preserves more serif detail. Short 7 px fits a smaller line. Changing square/circular LED preview cells does not change the actual sign's physical LEDs or glyph data. The sign is 32 columns wide, which is not much: in bold, TIME'S alone is too wide for it. Effect Text too wide for the sign Static, Flash then hold Must fit. Shorten the text or choose another effect; for Flash then hold the editor suggests Flash. Scroll long text Scrolls. Flash, Pulse Shows a few words at a time. Slide in, Countdown bar, Screen flash Scrolls on the sign. Automatic warnings Automatic rules live in Settings › Warnings & alerts and apply to all services and rehearsals . They trigger at time remaining , not time elapsed. In a ten-minute segment, a 01:30 rule triggers when 8 min 30 s have elapsed under ordinary uninterrupted timing. Warnings & alerts on a phone: four example warnings with their switches, a note on when a warning fires, then Phone alerts Example app preview · select to enlarge A new install has four warnings, for the operator and the stage. Use suggested warnings puts the suggested set back. At Warning On screens Stays up for 5:00 5 MIN LEFT White banner at the top 12 seconds 2:00 2 MIN LEFT Amber banner at the bottom 12 seconds 0:30 WRAP UP Amber banner at the bottom 10 seconds 0:00 TIME'S UP Flashes the screen red once, then stays red on the whole screen 10 seconds On the LED sign each scrolls, and stays up long enough to pass twice. When a warning fires. Each warning fires once in each segment, when the countdown comes down to its time. It never fires as a segment starts. A 5-minute segment does not begin with 5 MIN LEFT, and a 3-minute segment never shows it. A 6-minute segment shows it at 5:00. TIME'S UP at 0:00 still fires at zero. If you add time so that more is left than a warning's time, a warning that has not yet fired in this segment fires when the countdown comes down to it. One that has already fired does not fire again. Removing time past a warning's time fires it. Rehearsal speeds, phone notifications and Check this service follow the same rule. The check lists every warning that cannot fire in a segment; see Build a reusable program . Edit a warning Tap or click a warning, or Add , to open Edit warning or New warning . It is set out as questions. Edit warning on a PC, in two columns: When, 00:30 left with Change; What it shows, a preview with the LED sign and Stage screen switch and Edit text and style; Where, Operator only or Operator and stage; How long; On or off; Delete warning at the bottom left, Cancel and Save warning at the right Example app preview · select to enlarge Question What you set When The time left, in large figures and coloured as in the list. Change sets it. What it shows A preview that plays by itself, with the LED sign and Stage screen switch, a line saying how the text looks, and Edit text and style , which opens the same editor a cue has. Where Operator only : in the app and as a notification, while the stage keeps showing the timer. Operator and stage : also on the LED sign and stage screens, which then go back to the timer. How long Stays up for , up to 120 seconds. For text that scrolls, Scroll once, then back to the timer is offered too; while it is on, the time is set by one scroll. On or off Switch a warning off without deleting it. On a PC a wide window shows the editor in two columns, with Delete warning at the bottom left and Cancel and Save warning at the bottom right. On a phone the editor uses the whole screen, with Save at the top. Two warnings cannot share a time. If another warning already fires at the time you choose, the editor says so straight away and Save waits for a different time. Deleting still asks first. Edit warning on a phone: the whole screen, with Save at the top, then When, What it shows and Where Example app preview · select to enlarge A stage warning returns to the current countdown, or At zero, after its time. On the LED path, that time begins after the controller acknowledges it. New manual cues, Blank, Next and End service supersede a warning. Passed times are not replayed when rules change. If a manual Quick message covers every connected stage screen, automatic stage cues are consumed while it is present; phone warnings continue. With a targeted Quick message, other stage screens can still show warnings. Alerts on the phone Under Phone alerts , Clear phone warnings after is separate: choose 15, 30, 60 seconds or Until dismissed , with 30 seconds as default. A segment change or service end clears obsolete warning notices. This does not shorten stage warning duration or remove the active-service notification. Phone warnings use a distinct vibration pattern, which Wear OS watches mirror. Turn on Android notifications ( Turn on ) and Precise timing ( Allow ) where offered, then use Test on the Sound and vibration row. Volume, the notification channel and Do Not Disturb still affect sound. Background operation starts with the LED sign or sharing and keeps warnings running while locked; if Live says background operation is unavailable, keep the app open. Ready for service also shows whether Android battery optimisation could pause warnings with the screen off, with Allow to fix it. Force-stopping the app is not a supported way to silence a service. Alerts on a PC A PC shows a Windows notification at each warning and flashes the app's taskbar button. It plays no sound unless you turn on Play the Windows notification sound. The details are in Get started on Windows .

title: Send rich Quick messages
summary: Target stage screens, format the message and request explicit Seen.
text: Quick messages are for paired and web stage screens, with Phone, tablet or web screens as the destination. They are not for the LED sign. They let you send a longer, formatted instruction without changing the program. (The Send message tile in Stage & display is different: it sends a simple text message to whichever display is selected, the LED sign included. On a PC, M opens it.) Confirm sharing is on and the intended stage screens are approved and connected. On Live, in the Quick message section of Stage & display (shown while Phone, tablet or web screens is the destination), tap Write a message . In Send to , choose All connected stage screens , one screen, or a screen group. Only connected screens are listed; one that drops off while you write stays listed as "offline" and can't be picked. Write an optional headline and a message, or use Choose a preset and adapt it. The combined limit is 160 characters , with a headline of at most 48 and up to six message lines. Under Style , choose bold/italic, alignment, colour and text size. Set Show for on the wheel, or 00:00 for Until cleared. For a longer message, consider 15 or 30 seconds. Inspect the preview and recipient count. Optionally tick Request Seen acknowledgement . Use Test 5 s to check it reaches the screens in Send to, then tap Send message . Rich Quick message composer with recipient selection and formatting Example app preview · select to enlarge The recipients are fixed when you send. Newly joined or reconnected screens do not receive a replay of an earlier message. Other screens keep their normal output. When the message expires or you clear it, its recipients return to their current timer or preceding end/blank output. A segment change, manual cue, Blank, End service or disconnection can supersede the message. If Send is unavailable, the composer says why. Seen means a person tapped Mark seen. A transport acknowledgement only says the app received data. If you require acknowledgement, watch the "Seen N of M" count and per-recipient status. Web screens show the message but have no Seen button; they are listed as "On screen (web, no Seen)" and left out of the count. Do not assume silence means agreement, and do not repeatedly resend without checking the recipient list. Example stage message with an explicit Mark seen action Example app preview · select to enlarge Use Save preset , or Manage presets and Settings › Quick message presets , for repeatable messages with their formatting. Unsent Quick message drafts can be restored locally; restoring a draft never sends it. Sent messages are temporary and are not restored after restarting the app. After End service, messages can still be sent while approved stage screens remain connected and this device has control. The app asks you to confirm because the service has ended. Sending does not restart the service or change its report. Before any service has run, use Test 5 s or Test screen for setup rather than a normal Quick message.

title: Adjust the plan without losing control
summary: Review future timing changes and learn from comparable completed services.
text: Use Service timing overview to notice drift early. Its estimated finish assumes future segments use their allocations; pauses, overtime and manual advances can change the actual finish. Edit upcoming ( E on a PC) changes only future segments in this running service. It does not rewrite the current/completed segments, saved program or historical reports. Confirm changes with the service leader before shortening important activities. For a structured reduction, open Recover time from the Live rundown ( R on a PC). When the service is running behind, Commands suggests it first. Set Time to recover . Protect segments that must retain their duration (segments with Protect duration start protected). Choose Review adjustments and check each proposed before/after duration. Each remaining segment keeps at least one minute. Choose Apply reviewed adjustments only after the proposal is suitable. If the service/control state has changed, review again. Recover time review with protected segments and before/after durations Example app preview · select to enlarge Recover time changes allocations of upcoming segments for this running service only; it does not automatically move to the next segment or guarantee a finish time. The current segment keeps running. Future program defaults remain unchanged. After several comparable services, open Reports › ⋮ › Timing insights . The app requires at least three suitable observations and uses up to the five most recent comparable services for a program. It excludes rehearsals, Quick timers, incomplete/uncertain records, ambiguous segment names and paused time. Open in program editor appears when there is a suggestion. Suggestions use median active duration rounded up. In Program editor › Learn from previous services (offered only when past services can suggest a duration), select only the suggestions you want and Apply to draft , then save. These are planning aids, not instructions to rush a speaker or evidence of why a service ran long.

title: Finish and hand over cleanly
summary: End once, save the report and recover cleanly from a saving failure.
text: Confirm the service really is complete. Choose End service and confirm. In full screen, End service is in the control tray. Wait for the completed report to save. Live returns to the Standing by card ("Ready when you are") with Start service , Quick timer , Share to screens (or Manage sharing while sharing) and Join a service , and a Last service card with View last service report . The active rundown and timing overview disappear. Check the selected screen's end output: the program's end screen, or the clock if the program has no end screen. It remains connected. The Stage & display panel starts closed after a service; open it to blank or unblank, or to send a message or cue after the service. Open View last service report, check the service date and segment timings, add a review note if useful, and export or print if required. Stop sharing when the stage, viewer and web devices are no longer needed. Deliberately disconnect the LED if the equipment is being handed over or powered down. Full screen, on a phone, tablet or PC, stays open on the end screen, or the clock. Leave it with Exit in its tray, Esc or F11 ; it also closes when the next service is set up. On a PC, a second screen stays open on the end screen, or the clock, until you click Stop . The mini timer closes by itself when the service ends, and the countdown icon beside the Windows clock goes. Standing by on a phone after a saved service, with Start service, Quick timer and the Last service card Example app preview · select to enlarge If saving fails, the app retains the completed information and offers Retry saving report . Retry rather than starting a duplicate service. It preserves the original finish time and saves one report; a successful retry restores the Standing by card automatically. A pending save failure blocks service changes. Do not clear app storage to remove the message. An end screen belongs to the selected program. The Default end screen in Settings › Display settings seeds new programs and is used by Quick timers; changing that default does not overwrite existing program-specific end screens. No end screen: show the clock A program can end on the clock instead of an end screen. Choose Clock under When the service ends in the Program editor; see Build a reusable program . Settings › Display settings › Default end screen has the same choice, for new programs and Quick timers. Display settings on a PC: Default end screen, with When the service ends set to End screen, a preview of Hallelujah and Edit end screen Example app preview · select to enlarge When a service with no end screen ends: Every display shows the clock: the LED sign, paired phones and tablets, web screens, the second screen, full screen and both simulators, in the 12 or 24-hour format you chose. The End service question says so. It asks to "show the clock" where it would name the end screen, and with the LED sign it says the sign will show the clock. Live says Showing the clock . Show clock is greyed out, as the clock is already showing. Blank screen, cues and messages sent after the end go back to the clock when they are cleared. The button that would bring back the end screen says Back to clock . Every program, and the default, keeps its end screen until you choose Clock. Choosing End screen again in the default starts from "Hallelujah", ready to edit. A paired phone or tablet on an earlier version shows the clock too, but a backup or program file with this setting needs 0.35 or later to open.

title: Read, export and print reports
summary: Read the record, filter by date, add review notes, export it, and print the right copy with notes kept private.
text: Reports lists completed services as rows with a date badge, the length and start time, and an outcome chip: On time , N min over (amber) or N min under (blue), or "Partial" for an incomplete record. Rehearsals and saved Quick timers are labelled so they are not confused with real service timing. A finished service or segment is always on time, over or under in Reports; Live keeps "ahead" and "behind" for a service still running. Reports list on a phone with summary tiles, filters and outcome chips Example app preview · select to enlarge Above the list: Part What it shows Last live service tile How the latest live service compared with its plan, for example "1 min over". With several services it reads "Last N live services" and adds "avg". It leaves rehearsals out. On time tile How many of those services finished on time, for example "0 of 1". Most over tile The segment that ran over most. Search and Dates Find a service by name, or limit the date range. On a PC, Dates opens a calendar; see below. Filters All , Live only , Rehearsals , and Quick timers once one has been saved. List / Graph The Graph starts with bars of minutes over or under plan for the last few services, each date under its own bar. Tap a bar to see that service, for example "Ran 21 min · planned 25 min" with "4 min under", and Open report . Planned-vs-actual rows follow below. Open a row for its Service report : planned, actual, variance, paused time and time adjustments, then Print report at the foot of that summary card, Review notes , the Segment breakdown and the Activity timeline . Example report details and segment durations Example app preview · select to enlarge Reports on a PC In a desktop layout, your saved services are listed down the left, and the one you choose opens beside them. The newest report shows until you choose another. Reports on a PC: saved services on the left, the chosen report's planned and actual rows and segment table in the middle, review notes and the activity timeline on the right Example app preview · select to enlarge At the top: planned and actual time, how far over or under it ran, paused time and time adjustments. Planned against actual: a planned row above an actual row, with the part that ran over marked. With The dial layout it is a ring ending at the cross. The table: every segment with its planned time, actual time and a small bar showing whether it ran under or over. In a large window: review notes and the activity timeline sit beside the timings, and the Graph tab puts its summary beside the charts. Print report , export and review notes are all still there. Filter by date on a PC In a wide window, Dates opens a small calendar, Filter service dates , with two months side by side. Filter service dates on a PC: quick ranges on the left, October and November 2026 side by side with 28 October to 15 November selected, and Apply Example app preview · select to enlarge Click the first day, then the last. The days between fill in, and the range is written out in words above Apply . Or click a ready-made range: Last 4 weeks , This month , Last month , This year , or All dates , which clears the filter. Click Apply . A dot marks each day that has a saved report. Weeks start on Monday. The arrows beside the month names move between months. From the keyboard, the arrow keys move between days, Enter chooses, Page Up and Page Down change the month, and Esc cancels. A phone or a narrow window keeps the picker it had. Reading a report Read actual duration alongside planned and paused time. Activity records can help explain when an operator adjusted time, changed segment, answered a stage request or experienced a send failure; they do not prove what a person on stage saw. "Partial or uncertain timing" means the record should be reviewed before comparing it. Review notes are an after-service reflection, such as “Reduce the Announcements time from next week”, kept apart from the recorded timings. Use Add a review note (or Edit ). The note shows as "Last time" when the same program is next loaded into Ready, and is optional when exporting or printing. Export and share. A report's ⋮ menu has Export report CSV , Export report JSON and Delete report . To handle several, press and hold a row (click and hold on a PC) to select, then use Share (Bluetooth, messaging or email) or Export : pick a format (report file, spreadsheet or printable PDF) and whether to include review notes. JSON keeps richer report details. Reports › ⋮ › Export all reports covers every saved report. On a PC, Share and Export open the Windows Save window: one file is saved where you choose, and several go into a folder you choose. Deleting selected reports offers a 10-second Undo; Delete report and Delete all reports cannot be undone, so export first if you need a permanent copy. Print report is on a report; Print order of service is on program details and on Live (the print icon in the Service rundown header, and the Print button beside the program's summary on the Live home in a wide window). From a report, choose the Document : Service report or Service rundown. New records preserve the program snapshot, service date and church name used for that service, so editing today's program does not rewrite old speakers or notes. Older records may explicitly lack historical details. Print choices open as a sheet: Option Meaning Stage copy Excludes private notes. This is the appropriate starting point for distribution beyond the operator team. Operator copy Enables private notes; you may still untick Include private operator notes before printing. Review the content before sharing. Ink-saving Omits banner and watermark for this output. It is remembered from your last print. Church-name watermark A faint bold diagonal church name, used when a name exists. Ticking it turns Ink-saving off. Include church banner Uses the current configured banner; a historical service snapshot does not freeze the old image. Ticking it turns Ink-saving off. Include review notes Offered for a report that has one. Print order of service sheet with copy preset, banner and watermark Example app preview · select to enlarge The PDF repeats table headings and reserves footer space on every page for Church Service Timer · I-Proton and Page N of M . Service date and the document's preparation date/time/timezone are separate. Rundowns omit Planned start; historical reports retain useful planned/actual/paused columns. Choose Print to continue to Android's print screen, or the Windows print window on a PC, and select a printer or Save as PDF , or Share PDF to send the sheet directly. Review the destination and final pages. Printing a program before it has run offers a Service date . Its calendar reads the date the way the app writes it, "Fri 20 Nov 2026", starts the week on Monday and takes a typed date as 20/11/2026. A PDF is an exported copy; later app changes do not update a file already shared.

title: Make the workspace yours
summary: Set the church logo, name, banner and appearance; understand shared defaults.
text: Open Settings › Church profile , or tap the logo or mark at the top left of any page. A preview of the page header sits at the top, then three sections and one Save church profile button. Church profile on a phone with logo, church name and banner sections Example app preview · select to enlarge Section What to do Logo Choose logo , then crop it to a square: drag to move, pinch to zoom, then Use logo . It replaces the built-in mark at the top left of every page. Use built-in mark puts the original back. The home-screen app icon is unchanged. Church name Shown at the top of every page, on the opening screen and on new service reports. Services already loaded and older reports keep the name they had. Banner Choose banner , then crop it to its 3:1 shape (three times as wide as it is tall), so you choose which part of the photo shows. It is used on printed services and reports. Use built-in banner is always available. Choose a JPEG, PNG or WebP photo up to 5 MB and 40 megapixels. The app saves exactly what is inside the crop frame, and a transparent background stays transparent. Keep essential details away from the edges. The logo and banner are included in backups. Appearance offers thirteen preset themes and Create custom theme : Midnight Lime, Royal Navy, Warm Ivory, Deep Plum, Slate Teal, Morning Sky, Sage Linen, Ocean Deep, Cobalt Night, Graphite (clean white, for dark booths), Paper & Ink (near-black ink, for well-lit rooms), Paper & Ink (blue) (ink-blue buttons) and Meadow. Preview the choice, then Save appearance ; Cancel or Back discards the preview. Test readability in the actual room, including overtime and warning labels. A beautiful palette is not useful if the operator cannot distinguish a warning at a glance. Appearance settings on a phone with selectable theme tiles Example app preview · select to enlarge The Layout & accessibility tab sets the Desktop layout ( Tablet layout on a 10-inch or larger tablet; a phone has neither), Show keyboard keys on buttons and Saved looks (all three are described in Run the service from a PC ), then Layout density (Compact, Comfortable, Spacious or Automatic, the default), High contrast , Reduced motion and the divider style. With Reduced motion on, a cue that slides in simply appears, and Screen flash gives the screen a coloured edge instead of a flash. On a PC or a large tablet, Settings › Desktop layout (or Tablet layout ) opens straight on this tab and names the layout in use, and the Theme tab has a button that switches to it. Other useful settings: Setting Scope At zero Display settings. Shared by every service: Show 00:00 or Custom text . Default end screen Display settings. End screen or Clock , for new programs and Quick timers; existing programs keep their own setting. Clock format Display settings. 12 or 24 hour for the clock on stage, and the Blinking colon on paired and web screens (on by default). Times you choose in the app, such as the pre-service countdown, are always 24-hour. LED preview shape Display settings. Square or circular visual cells; does not reconfigure physical hardware. Desktop layout, or Tablet layout How Live is arranged in a wide window: Mission control, Three panes, The dial, Keys or Classic. Not shown on a phone or a small tablet. Warnings & alerts Shared rules; phone alerts, or Alerts on this computer on a PC; lock-screen controls; clicker and foot pedal, and its test page. Stage cues Shared prepared cue buttons, with their effect and their formatting for the LED sign and for screens. Quick message presets Saved rich messages for stage screens. Screens & devices Pairing, saved devices, web screens and what web stage displays show, Requests from the stage, the Second screen on a PC, and Full screen on this phone. Keep screen awake Prevents sleep while the app is visible; it is not a guarantee against force-stop or power loss. Settings PIN Optional lock for Settings, deleting and sign administration. See Protect data and manage the LED device . About Installed version, creator I-Proton, What's new, Check for updates, Check for updates automatically, Your data, Privacy policy, Guided practice, Diagnostics and the open-source licences. Use Search settings at the top of Settings to find a page by name; "layout" finds Desktop layout on a PC, or Tablet layout on a large tablet, and "keyboard" finds Keyboard shortcuts. Settings in a wide window. The groups sit in two columns. Appearance keeps its preview beside the themes and layouts. Display settings lists its sections down the left. Warnings & alerts and Stage cues show what your display will show. Church profile, Backup & restore, Feedback centre, Settings PIN, About, Diagnostics and Ready for service each put a preview or a summary beside the settings. The simulator display profile is a preview assumption until supported hardware is connected and validated. Do not interpret a manually set preview width as a measurement of an unknown sign.

title: Connection recovery and troubleshooting
summary: Diagnose a stale screen, lost connection, missing warning or rejected command, on a phone or a PC.
text: Start with the destination badge, not repeated button presses. Identify whether the problem is the device's network, the app's connection, a held output, or the receiver itself. Displays, pairing and timing Symptom Check / next action Arc counts, LED is unchanged Confirm LED sign is selected, the device is on sign Wi-Fi, and the connection is authenticated. Inspect "Output paused after an interruption"; review and Restore current output when offered. App disconnects while the device remains on Wi-Fi Live shows "Reconnecting to LED sign" with Reconnect display and Stop trying ; timer controls and cues stay usable, and the sign receives current output when it returns. Re-enter credentials only if missing or rejected; do not change passwords as the first troubleshooting step. LED counts after Wi-Fi is off Expected for an accepted native countdown. Reconnect before expecting new cues, pause/resume or a new segment to reach it. One brief blink at a change Expected on the tested W2 during program replacement. Repeated blinking while a steady timer should run needs investigation. The sign did not acknowledge "Blanking was not acknowledged" means the previous sign may still show its last output; you can still switch with Leave output . A cue showing "Not sent" did not reach the sign. Check the sign itself and its connection before resending. Timing was recovered with uncertainty After a restart or long interruption the app asks you to Verify remaining time . Check and correct it, then Verify & restore . The service report keeps its uncertainty marker. Pairing host is not found Same Wi-Fi, host sharing on, no client isolation. Try Scan QR code instead if discovery alone fails. QR cannot fix blocked phone-to-phone traffic. Phones on a hotspot can't see each other Some sign hotspots, guest Wi-Fi and church networks keep devices apart. Use the host device's own hotspot and join the other devices to it. The host shares again at the new address by itself. A browser can't open the web screen Use the QR code or the address instead of the easy name (some devices do not open .local names). Check the browser is on the same Wi-Fi and the host is still sharing. On a Windows laptop, the easy name may not work while its Wi-Fi is set to a Public network ; use the address, or set that network to Private in Windows settings. If a printed address stopped working, the host got a new address: export the join slide again. A stage screen shows only a waiting message The display is still set to the Simulator or the LED sign. Select Show on stage screens in the note on Live. Mobile preview looks frozen/stale Receiver may be disconnected. Keep its app open, check network and Saved devices, then reconnect. Do not treat stale output as a live countdown. Cue command is rejected Check who has control and whether the program, segment or selected cue changed. Review the current service instead of repeatedly pressing an old control. Warning not visible on stage Check the warning is switched on, its time, Where (it must be Operator and stage ) and the connection. Intentional Blank suppresses stage warnings; all-screen Quick messages can take priority. A warning never shows in a short segment A warning set for the whole of a segment, or for longer, cannot fire: 5 MIN LEFT does not show in a 5-minute or a 3-minute segment. Run Check this service to list every warning that cannot fire. A cue will not save: its text is too wide for the LED sign Static and Flash then hold must fit the sign. Shorten the text, or choose Scroll long text , or Flash or Pulse , which show long text a few words at a time. The stage shows only the next segment's name, not who and how long That paired phone or tablet is on an earlier version, or the screen is set to another layout. Update it, and choose Timer and up next . No notification sound Check Android permission, channel sound, volume, Do Not Disturb and Precise timing. Use Test under Sound and vibration. Warnings stop or the timer notification goes quiet with the screen off Battery optimisation may pause warnings. Tap the battery hint on Live, or Allow on the Battery row in Ready for service, to open the Android setting. If background operation is unavailable, keep the app open. In full screen, a tap only shows Hold to unlock The controls are locked. With Lock controls on, the gestures, the tray and every key do nothing. Hold to unlock , then try again. The tray in full screen goes away It hides after 6 seconds untouched. Tap or click once, swipe up from the bottom edge, or move the mouse to the bottom of the screen to bring it back. It stays while the mouse is on it. A double tap in full screen asked the wrong question The left third asks Undo, the middle Pause or Resume, the right third Next segment. Choose Cancel ; nothing changes until you confirm. The screens show the clock after End service, not an end screen The program is set to end on the Clock . Open the program, and under When the service ends choose End screen . For new programs and Quick timers, change Settings › Display settings › Default end screen . An earlier version refuses a backup or program file A program in it, or the default, is set to end on the Clock, which needs 0.35 or later. Update that device. Full screen is still showing after the service ended That is intended: it shows the end screen, or the clock. Leave with Exit in the tray, Esc or F11 . It closes by itself when the next service is set up. No update notice, though Check for updates automatically is on The check runs at most once a day and never during a service or while the controls are locked. The notice shows only on Live while standing by, and Not now hides it for that version. Offline, the check says nothing. Tap Check for updates to check now. Screen is blank but timer runs Check for intentional Blank. Tap Unblank screen , or choose Show timer as appropriate. Quick message send is disabled Phone, tablet or web screens destination, sharing, connected recipients in Send to and control are needed. The composer says which is missing. Before the first run, use Test 5 s . Controller administration is disabled Connect to sign Wi-Fi and authenticate the supported LED display; end the service and stop sharing. Report save fails Use Retry saving report . Keep the completed information; do not clear data or create a duplicate run. Cannot find timing suggestions At least three comparable completed services are needed. Rehearsals, Quick timers, ambiguous names and incomplete/uncertain records are excluded. On a Windows PC Symptom Check / next action Windows protected your PC The installer is not code-signed. Click More info , then Run anyway . Live looks like the phone app, or uses Classic whatever layout is chosen The window is narrower than 1200 or shorter than 600, or the focused operator view is on. Widen or maximise the window; Classic is set out to work well if you cannot. Windows display scaling counts: a 1366 × 768 screen at 125% gives a window about 1093 wide. On a tablet, turn it to landscape and let the app fill the screen. "No second screen connected" Check the cable, then press Windows + P and choose Extend . With Duplicate there is only one screen to show on. The second screen did not open when the service started Live says why: no screen has been chosen yet, or the screen used last time is not connected. Click Show on second screen once to choose it. The line of keys is missing It shows only while Show keyboard keys on buttons is on, and not in a window 600 high. Classic has no line; it shows each key on its button. A key does nothing Check the controls are not locked, the cursor is not in a text field, Live is the page showing, no dialog is open, and a service is running. Press ? for the list. Space and Page Down do nothing, but other keys work Clicker and foot pedal is switched off in Settings › Warnings & alerts. On a PC that turns those keys off on the keyboard too. A clicker does nothing Check Clicker and foot pedal is switched on. Then open Test a clicker or pedal to see which key each button sends. Check for updates offers only Open release page That release has no Windows installer. Download what the page lists and install it yourself. Download and install says to finish the service first An update cannot be installed while a service runs. End the service, then try again. No warning notification Windows holds notifications back under Do not disturb , which it turns on by itself when the screen is duplicated. The taskbar button still flashes. Use Test in Warnings & alerts. Warnings make no sound That is the default on a PC. Turn on Play the Windows notification sound if you want it. The countdown icon is missing beside the clock It shows only while a service or Quick timer runs. On Windows 11 look behind the small arrow and drag it out. Check Show the countdown in the notification area is on. A dropped file is refused Drop one program file ( .json or .csv ) at a time. A drop is refused while a service is running or the controls are locked. Phones cannot reach the PC host Allow the app through Windows Defender Firewall on private networks, and check the PC's network is set to Private. The mini timer or full screen will not open Full screen needs a running service or Quick timer, and cannot be opened once the service has ended; the mini timer needs neither. Neither opens from the other. Unlock the controls first. How recovery works The LED connection tolerates brief health-check misses before reconnecting. Retry delay rises from about two to thirty seconds. Within the same trusted active service, recovery restores the latest intended output against the original deadline; it does not replay every missed update. Deliberate Disconnect, Forget this sign, or another output selection stops LED retries. A saved credential does not override that choice. Restarting the app, uncertain timing, a long absence or an existing output hold can require review before restoration. For an interruption during worship: keep one responsible operator in control, establish what the stage is actually seeing, restore connectivity, check the timer against the real activity, and restore current output once. A second person should not open another independent LED app and compete for the sign.

title: Protect data and manage the LED device
summary: Back up your setup, move it between a phone and a PC, and understand the boundaries of LED administration.
text: Use Settings › Backup & restore › Export backup before changing devices or replacing a setup. Backups include saved programs (with version history), the segment library, cues, reports, preferences, saved looks and the church profile, including the logo and reduced banner. A backup moves between a phone and a PC. One made on either restores on the other, so you can build programs on the office PC and run them from a phone, or the other way round. Keep exports containing private notes in an appropriate place. Saved sign passwords are left out unless you tick Include saved passwords , which encrypts them with a Passphrase you choose. Restoring asks for that passphrase; skipping it or a wrong passphrase still restores everything else. Restoring replaces saved data on the target device after review ( Restore and replace ). A backup from before 0.34 has its untouched starting cues and warnings brought up to the new suggested set, as an update does; any you changed are kept. Export its current setup first if it should be kept. Backups do not transfer an active clock, phone permissions, pairing approvals, the Settings PIN, received programs waiting for review, local editing drafts or a live display connection. Some choices also stay with the device: the desktop or tablet layout in use, what the Simulator simulates and shows, the second screen and full screen choices, the Check for updates automatically switch, and a PC's notification sound and countdown icon switches. Reconnect and approve equipment again as needed. Settings PIN (optional, 4–8 digits) locks Settings, deleting programs and reports, and LED sign administration; Live, Programs and Reports stay open. Setting it shows a one-time recovery code that removes the PIN if forgotten ( Forgot PIN? ). Settings lock again whenever the app leaves the screen. Turn off PIN removes it. LED device management is for the sign, not the phone, tablet or PC. It shows the saved Wi-Fi password and Connection password , with Show on each row and change or forget in the row's ⋮ menu. Once connected, Open Wi-Fi and Details help reach the correct network and controller. Revealing a saved password shows the app's local copy; it does not retrieve an unknown current password from the sign. Saving a known Wi-Fi password locally does not change the sign's Wi-Fi configuration. Changing the sign's Wi-Fi name or passwords requires a supported authenticated LED connection, the correct Wi-Fi, an ended service and stopped sharing. Reserve this for the equipment administrator outside a live service. Keep the current and intended new details available until reconnection verifies the change. The administration setters have automated/packet validation, but physical password/Wi-Fi write-and-reconnect acceptance remains outstanding for this build. A controller acknowledgement is not proof that a new password works after reconnection. If there is "No acknowledgement", the setting may have changed: rejoin using the new details first, and do not repeatedly apply the change. Do not alter scan, polarity or firmware settings as part of normal operator onboarding. For help, open Settings › Feedback centre . Enter a title, a message and your contact. Include optional diagnostics can be reviewed before inclusion. Open email app opens a draft to immanuelproton@gmail.com ; you must send it in your email app. On a PC it opens the PC's email program, and a long message is put on the clipboard with a note to paste it. Copy feedback is the fallback. No automatic support delivery or response time is promised. Describe the app version, output type, steps, expected result and actual result. Avoid including passwords, pairing QR codes or private speaker notes. Copy important text before closing the form. For a performance problem, Settings › About › Diagnostics › Record service metrics records the next service on this device (memory, battery, smoothness, timer accuracy, warning timing and reconnections), then switches itself off. It records no service content or people, and nothing leaves the device until you tap Share recording .

title: Trainer session and readiness checklist
summary: Coach a new operator through a practical session and a readiness checklist.
text: Suggested coached session: 10 minutes explaining roles and output, 15 minutes of simulator practice (guided practice is a good start), 15 minutes on the actual connected equipment (the PC, projector and clicker included, if you use them), then 10 minutes of recovery and reporting. These are teaching estimates, not app timers. Before the service Confirm the installed version on every phone, tablet and PC, and the program, speakers, allocations and what it shows when it ends: an end screen or the clock. Choose the intended destination and confirm the physical screen with another person. Check power, battery optimisation on phones, network reachability and notification sound. On a PC: set Windows to Extend , click Show on second screen and look at the projector. Decide whether warnings should play the Windows sound; they are silent unless you turn it on. Test the clicker or pedal on Test a clicker or pedal , and tell whoever holds it what each button does. Review shared warning times and prepared cues with the service leader. Run Check this service on the program and read the list of warnings that cannot fire. Agree who hosts and who has control; name and approve receivers deliberately. If browsers will follow, check the guest code, team code and join slide are current. Open ⋮ › Ready for service on Live to review the app checklist. An isolated simulator test is not proof of physical delivery. Review stage-message recipients and screen groups; do not use a real congregation-facing screen for an unannounced test. During the service Watch both the current segment and the whole-service timing overview. Use Next when the real activity changes; do not rely on automatic advance. Read confirmation dialogs before time adjustments or ending. On a PC, a key asks first too. Lock the controls when you step away; unlock with Hold to unlock. Keep cues concise; target rich messages carefully and distinguish delivery from Seen. Answer stage requests promptly with Acknowledge, Dismiss or Add 2 min. Check any disconnected/stale/held indication before assuming output is current. Keep the host powered; control handover does not move the service to another device. Do not close the app's window on a PC during the service. After the service End once, confirm the report saved, and inspect View last service report. Add a review note while it is fresh. Print or export the right copy; inspect private-note inclusion before distribution. Stop sharing, stop the second screen, leave full screen, and deliberately disconnect equipment when appropriate. Record an issue or useful program improvement. Back up the configuration after significant changes. Competency drills Ask the learner to demonstrate each task with the simulator first: Drill Successful result Load without starting Explains Ready, shows that the timer in Ready is not counting, and starts only after checking the destination. Pause versus blank Shows that Pause stops time while Blank only hides output. Cue and return Sends a prepared cue and returns to the current countdown. Overtime transition Recognises red overtime and starts the next segment correctly. Quick timer Starts a named 10 min timer, explains Save as a report, and ends it with End timer. Message targeting Names the recipients, sends a temporary message and explains Seen. Recover time Protects a segment, reviews changes and explains that the saved program is unchanged. Connection interruption Distinguishes network from app state and reviews before restoring output. Close and print Saves a single report and produces a Stage copy without private notes. Keyboard run (PC) Pauses with Space and confirms, advances with Page Down twice, sends cue 1 and returns to the timer, and shows that Lock controls blocks every key. Second screen (PC) Shows the stage on the projector, changes what it shows, and stops it with Stop or Esc. Full screen Opens full screen, pauses with a double tap or double-click in the middle and confirms in the card, opens the tray and sends a cue, shows that Lock controls blocks the gestures and the tray, and leaves with Esc or Exit. Full screen at the end Ends the service from the tray, explains why full screen stays on the end screen or the clock, and leaves it. End on the clock Sets a program to end on the Clock, reads the End service question, and shows where to change the default for new programs and Quick timers. Cue on screens Makes a cue an amber banner at the bottom, gives it an effect, and checks it with the LED sign and Stage screen preview switch. Check this service Runs the check on a program, names a warning that cannot fire and says why, and explains that nothing reached the stage. Warning editor Adds a warning, chooses Operator only or Operator and stage, and explains when it fires. The learner should be able to perform the routine controls and explain when to call the experienced operator. Repeat the exact church equipment setup before independent operation; a simulator pass alone is not the equipment check.

title: Quick reference and knowledge check
summary: Look up terms, check your understanding and review the current scope.
text: Term Remember it as Program The reusable plan, not the running service. Segment One timed activity inside a program. Ready Loaded and reviewed, but not counting yet. On a PC it shows your layout's own timer with the first segment's full time. Quick timer A single countdown with no program or Ready step; saved only if you choose. Host The device that owns the service clock, saving and output: a phone, a tablet or a PC. Stage cue A prepared one-tap instruction with saved formatting, for the LED sign and for screens. Effect How a cue behaves: static, scroll, flash, flash then hold, pulse, slide in, countdown bar or screen flash. Automatic warning A cue the app shows by itself, once in each segment, when the countdown reaches its time. Check this service A quick run through a program on the Simulator that lists every warning and flags any that cannot fire. Up next The line under a stage countdown that says who is next and for how long. Quick message A richer temporary message for selected stage screens. Web screen A browser on the same Wi-Fi following the service; it cannot control it. Second screen A projector or monitor plugged into the PC, showing the stage full screen with no pairing. Full screen The stage countdown on the screen of the device running the service, with gestures and a control tray to run the service from it. Control tray The row of buttons along the bottom of full screen. A tap, a swipe up or the mouse at the bottom edge opens it; it hides after 6 seconds. LED simulator / Stage simulator The Simulator pretending to be an LED sign or a stage screen. Neither sends to hardware. Desktop layout, or Tablet layout How Live is arranged in a wide window: Mission control, Three panes, The dial, Keys or Classic. Mini timer A small always-on-top window on a PC with the countdown, Pause, Next and one cue; with no service, the time of day. Check for updates automatically An optional check, at most once a day and never during a service. Off to begin with. It only shows a notice on Live. Commands A searchable list of everything you can do now, opened with Ctrl+K on a PC. Banner A cue shown in a band at the top or bottom of a screen while the countdown stays in view. Guest code / team code The guest code opens Order of service and stays the same each week; the team code also opens Stage display and Service overview, and changes each time you share. At zero Shared output behaviour when a segment expires. End screen The selected program's output after End service. A program set to Clock has no end screen and shows the time of day. Controller accepted / Stage screens received Data acknowledged by the receiver; not optical verification. Seen An explicit human acknowledgement on a paired stage screen. Disconnect Pause access/connection without necessarily forgetting saved identity. Forget Remove saved approval or credentials; setup is needed again. Check your understanding If the main arc moves, does that prove the LED sign is current? No. Check connection/acknowledgement and the physical output. Does Blank screen pause the countdown? No. It hides output while time continues. A ten-minute segment has a warning at 01:30. When does it trigger? At 1 min 30 s remaining, normally 8 min 30 s after starting. Will a newly reconnected receiver replay a Quick message sent earlier? No. Recipients are fixed at send time and missed messages are not replayed. Does changing the default end screen update all saved programs? No. Edit an existing program's own end screen. Can a second operator take control just by pairing? No. The host must approve it and grant control explicitly. What do you do if End service cannot save its report? Use Retry saving report; preserve the completed information. Should a Stage print copy include private notes? No. Operator copy is a separate deliberate choice. Does a Quick timer appear in Reports? Only if Save as a report was turned on; then it is marked Quick timer. Can someone with the guest code see the stage countdown in a browser? No. The guest code opens only Order of service; Stage display needs the team code. On a PC, does pressing Space pause the service at once? No. It asks first; Space or Enter confirms and Esc cancels. With Lock controls on, which keys still work? None. Every key is blocked until you Hold to unlock. Does a warning play a sound on a PC? Not unless Play the Windows notification sound is turned on. A notification appears and the taskbar button flashes. Does a projector plugged into the PC need pairing? No. Set Windows to Extend and click Show on second screen. A cue is set to Banner at the bottom. What does the LED sign show? The cue as before. Colour, banners, Wrap long text and Speed on screens change screens only. The chip reads Stage simulator. Is anything reaching the stage? No. Either simulator is a preview on your own device. A five-minute segment has a warning at 05:00. When does it show? Never. A warning fires only when the countdown comes down to its time, not as a segment starts. Does Check this service send anything to the LED sign or the stage screens? No. It runs on the Simulator only, changes nothing on Live and saves no report. On a PC, Clicker and foot pedal is switched off. Does Space still pause? No. A PC cannot tell a clicker from its keyboard, so Space, B, Page Down and → do nothing. The buttons on screen still work. A cue uses Slide in and its text is too wide for the LED sign. What does the sign show? It scrolls the text. Screens slide it in. In full screen, you double tap the right third of the screen. Does the service go to the next segment at once? No. It asks first, like every timer action. With Lock controls on, it does nothing at all. The service ends while full screen is open. What does that screen show? The end screen, or the clock if the program has no end screen. Full screen stays open, Cues, Clock, Blank and Exit still work, and it closes when the next service is set up. Check for updates automatically is switched on. Will the app install an update by itself? No. It checks at most once a day, never during a service, and only shows a notice on Live. Nothing is downloaded or installed without asking. A service is loaded on a PC and the ring shows 05:00. Is it counting? No. That is Ready: the layout's own timer with the first segment's full time. Nothing counts until Start first segment. A program is set to end on the Clock. What do the LED sign and the stage screens show after End service? The clock, on every display. Live says Showing the clock, and Show clock is greyed out. Current scope This guide covers version 0.35.0 on Android and Windows. 0.35.0 is the next release; until it is published, the download page gives 0.34.0, which does not have what the release notes list under 0.35.0. An iOS or Mac app and universal LED compatibility are not provided; browsers can only follow a service as web screens, never control it. The original Matrix glyphs and square-matrix glyphs are unchanged. Tinos is bundled; installed/imported font loading is not part of the workflow. LED countdowns, segments and Quick timers stay within 59:59. Physical checks have established the supported W2 countdown, expected one-blink transitions, scrolling warnings returning to the current timer, and Next segment after overtime. Full-service endurance, power-loss acceptance and controller administration writes still require controlled hardware validation. Web screens, guided practice, Quick timer, stage requests and the other features added from 0.19 to 0.35 are described here from the app's release notes and on-screen wording; behaviour on your phones, PCs, routers, browsers and projectors has not been verified by this handbook, so hands-on testing of that release remains the user's responsibility. The Windows app is new. Its installer is not code-signed, so Windows warns before it runs. The second screen, the mini timer, full screen, the countdown beside the clock and Download and install depend on how Windows, your graphics driver and your screens behave. Rehearse the exact PC, projector and clicker before a service, and keep a phone with the same programs as a fallback. The online handbook and this Markdown guide are training materials, not a remote-control interface. Nothing in the handbook can connect to a sign, start a service or send a stage cue.
